title: DECISION: where do v2's login funnel events go?
description:
Owner decision. wt-ksh.12.7 built the instrumentation but deliberately did not choose a destination, because v2 has NO analytics dependency at all today (verified 2026-08-18: no logsnag, posthog or analytics anywhere in v2/src or v2/convex) and wiring one needs a credential and a vendor call that are not mine to make.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: v2/src/lib/funnel.ts emits four typed events — login_view, login_provider_click (with provider), login_code_requested, login_callback_arrived (oauth|otp). All four call sites are wired and verified firing. The module is destination-agnostic: shipping them somewhere is a change to the single send() function and nothing else. Today send() logs to console in dev and no-ops in production, so NOTHING IS BEING COLLECTED YET and wordle-teams-390 still cannot be attributed.

OPTIONS:
 (a) LogSnag. The v2 design says 'keep LogSnag', v1 already emits to it, and one destination is what makes the v1-vs-v2 funnel directly comparable — which is the whole point of measuring. Needs an API token in the Worker env. CAUTION: v1's handleLogsnagEvent awaits logsnag.track() with no try/catch so an outage blocks sign-in (wordle-teams-4ov); funnel.ts is already written fire-and-forget, so do not reintroduce that shape.
 (b) A Convex table. Zero new vendors, queryable with the tools already in the project, and at ~200 login views a month the volume is negligible. Weigh against wordle-teams-dcu (database bandwidth, not function calls, is the binding free-tier limit) — though at this volume that is noise.
 (c) Cloudflare Web Analytics. Already in the v2 design, but it is page-level and cannot see a provider-button click, so it does not answer wordle-teams-390 on its own.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) LogSnag, precisely because comparability with v1's existing funnel is the thing that makes the number actionable.

DO NOT PUT EMAIL ADDRESSES IN THESE EVENTS. The repo is public and the payload may reach a third party; funnel.ts documents this rule and currently carries provider ids and step names only.
acceptance_criteria: A destination is chosen, funnel.ts's send() ships to it fire-and-forget, and a real login on beta produces a visible login_view and login_callback_arrived pair.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-18. LogSnag chosen and wired end to end, verified on beta.

SHAPE. The token is a secret and cannot ship to the browser, so the client beacons to a new /api/funnel route and the Worker forwards to LogSnag. Project 'wordle-teams' (same as v1, which is what keeps the two funnels comparable) on its own channel 'login-funnel' with notify:false, so it does not drown v1's signup notifications on 'users'. Delivered by fetch rather than the logsnag package — one less dependency, a few lines on a Worker.

VERIFIED ON BETA, not locally. An x-funnel response header reports sent | skipped | dropped:
  login_view                -> sent
  login_provider_click      -> sent
  login_callback_arrived    -> sent
  unknown event name        -> dropped
  malformed body            -> dropped
Also confirmed the browser actually beacons: loading beta's /login produced POST /api/funnel {"name":"login_view"} and clicking Google produced the provider_click. And the exact payload shape was accepted directly by api.logsnag.com with HTTP 200.

WHY THE HEADER EXISTS. A 204 alone cannot distinguish 'delivered' from 'quietly dropped because LOGSNAG_TOKEN is unset on the Worker' — the unconfigured path returns early and reports nowhere, so it was the one silent failure mode in the design. The header makes it curl-checkable without changing the beacon contract, since clients ignore response headers. That is how I proved the Worker can actually read the secret.

keepalive ON THE CLIENT FETCH. login_provider_click fires immediately before the document navigates away to the provider, so a normal fetch would be cancelled — precisely the event that tells us someone chose a provider would be the one most likely lost.

SECURITY. /api/funnel is public and unauthenticated. Event names, providers and methods are allowlisted and tags are BUILT rather than passed through, so nothing from the request body reaches LogSnag verbatim and no PII is carried (these events are pre-auth anyway). The mapping is a pure function with 7 unit tests — which is how a real bug got caught: with an object literal, EVENTS['__proto__'] resolves up the prototype chain to Object.prototype, which is truthy, so the allowlist passed for a name that was never allowed and emitted an event with an undefined name. It is a Map now.

NEVER BLOCKS AUTH. The route always answers 204 and never throws; an unset token is a silent no-op; LogSnag failures go to Sentry. wordle-teams-4ov is exactly the opposite shape in v1 — an awaited logsnag.track() with no try/catch, where a vendor outage blocks sign-in.

CONFIG. LOGSNAG_TOKEN pushed with 'wrangler secret put' to the wordle-teams-v2 Worker (verified present via 'wrangler secret list'); the value came from the repo root .env.local and is not in git. ENVIRONMENT is now a declared wrangler var set to 'beta' — CHANGE IT TO 'production' AT CUTOVER (Phase 8) or every prod event will be tagged beta.

NOTE: the verification above wrote a handful of synthetic events into the login-funnel channel today, plus one 'Funnel wiring check'. Ignore them when reading early numbers.

STILL OPEN, and this is the point of the whole exercise: wordle-teams-390 cannot be attributed until real traffic flows through beta. The events exist now; the data does not yet.
close_reason: Closed

title: Write the v2 addendum to docs/design-system/
description:
Add a short v2-targeting addendum to docs/design-system/ so the bundle stops misleading readers.

The bundle as exported reads as though it targets the replatform, but every file path,
Tailwind version and component assumption in it is v1's. A future session that opens
MIGRATION.md and follows it will edit the wrong app.

Write docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md recording: that MIGRATION.md and globals.v2.css are
v1-targeted and were NOT run; how the token set was actually translated to Tailwind v4; the
decisions taken (supersede the teal palette, adopt shadcn on the radix base); and where the v2
tokens now live. Leave the original export files unmodified — they are the diff baseline for
future revisions in Claude Design.
acceptance_criteria: docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md exists and states that MIGRATION.md is v1-targeted and was not run; the original export files are unmodified.
close_reason: docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md written. Records that MIGRATION.md and globals.v2.css are v1-targeted and were not run; the four deliberate token deviations and why; the --accent-foreground double-declaration and rename; the Tailwind 4 layer structure and why Layer 3 is permanent in v2; the supersede/shadcn/font decisions; the broken radix-nova style; what the bundle does not cover; the wt-ksh.12.10 board bug; and a file map. Original export files verified unmodified — git shows only the new file.

title: Login surface: labeled provider buttons + funnel events (A7 exception)
description:
Spend the A7 parity exception: the login/onboarding surface.

This is the one surface where this phase may change behaviour, not just appearance. Amendment
A7 (2026-08-18) granted it because wordle-teams-390 is the product's largest measured leak —
~93% of people who reach /login never complete an auth round-trip, with ZERO server-side auth
failures in either measurement window, and the leak did not move when Lemon Squeezy was removed.

Two deliverables, both from wordle-teams-390's acceptance criteria:

1. LABELED PROVIDER BUTTONS. v1 renders a 3x2 grid of icon-only buttons whose labels exist only
   as sr-only text plus a hover Tooltip (src/app/login/oauth/oauth-provider.tsx:50-67). Tooltips
   do not appear on tap, and the heaviest login traffic is iPhone. v2 ships visible text labels.

2. CLIENT-SIDE FUNNEL EVENTS: login-page view, provider-button click, callback arrival — enough
   to attribute where abandonment happens rather than inferring it from server logs.

OPEN ITEM, decide before building #2: v2 has no analytics dependency at all today (checked
2026-08-18 — no logsnag, posthog or analytics anywhere in v2/src or v2/convex). The v2 design
says 'keep LogSnag' and adds Cloudflare Web Analytics. Recommend LogSnag since v1 already emits
to it and comparing v1 and v2 funnels against one destination is the entire point of measuring.
Note v1's handleLogsnagEvent has a known unguarded-await bug (wordle-teams-4ov) — do not port
that shape; fire and forget, never block auth on the analytics call.

DESIGN_SYSTEM.md gives no guidance on the provider grid. It documents the OTP input and nothing
else about this surface, so this is additive work the bundle does not hand us.
acceptance_criteria: beta's login screen shows visible text labels on every provider button, and login-page view, provider-button click and callback arrival all emit to the chosen destination without blocking auth.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-18, with one part deliberately left open (see the end).

A7 EXCEPTION SPENT ON THE LOGIN SURFACE. The page went from unstyled raw HTML to a real product login: Card, labelled Input, primary Send code button, a divider, and four FULL-WIDTH LABELLED provider buttons. Screenshotted at 390x844 in both themes.

FINDING THAT SHRANK HALF THIS TASK: v2 never inherited v1's icon-only tooltip grid. v1 renders a 3x2 grid of icon-only buttons whose labels exist only as sr-only text plus a hover Tooltip, and tooltips do not appear on tap while the heaviest login traffic is iPhone. v2's login was already rendering the literal words Google / Microsoft / GitHub / Discord. So the labelled-buttons half of wordle-teams-390 was structurally satisfied before I started; this task made them look like buttons rather than adding the labels. Added a comment at SOCIAL_PROVIDERS so nobody 'restores parity' by reducing them to icons.

FUNNEL EVENTS: four, all wired and verified firing — login_view (once per mount, post-hydration, so it counts real browsers not SSR or crawlers), login_provider_click (emitted BEFORE the redirect, since nothing on /login runs again once the provider takes the document), login_code_requested, and login_callback_arrived. Callback arrival needed a mechanism: the OAuth round-trip finishes as a fresh document load, so /login cannot observe it. callbackURL now carries ?signin=oauth (and the OTP path ?signin=otp); the landing page reads it, emits, and strips it with replaceState so a refresh cannot double-count.

funnel.ts is written to two hard rules, both documented in-file: never block or fail auth (wordle-teams-4ov is exactly that bug in v1 — an awaited logsnag.track() with no try/catch), and never carry PII, since the repo is public.

REGRESSION I CAUGHT BECAUSE I TOOK A BASELINE FIRST. I ran the e2e suite BEFORE touching anything (2/2 green), which made the next failure unambiguous: shadcn's CardTitle renders a plain <div>, so wrapping the page in a Card silently left /login with NO <h1> and broke the heading-role assertion. That is an accessibility defect, not just a test-selector problem — any page using Card as its main region loses its heading. Fixed by adding asChild to CardTitle (Slot-based, documented) so callers can supply the right heading level while keeping the styling. e2e now 2/2 again, and I confirmed a clean run has zero errors — an SSR trace I saw in one run was a transient mid-recompile artifact and does not reproduce.

wt-ksh.2.2 PRESERVED. Email input still uncontrolled and read via FormData; submits still disabled until hydrated. The OTP field is now controlled because InputOTP owns its value — safe, and noted in the file, because the code step only mounts after an explicit click and so never exists pre-hydration. The no-JavaScript regression test still passes.

LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE — wt-ksh.12.11. The events have NO DESTINATION. v2 has no analytics dependency at all and choosing one needs a credential and a vendor decision that are the owner's, not mine. send() logs in dev and no-ops in production, so nothing is being collected yet and wordle-teams-390 still cannot be attributed until that lands. funnel.ts is destination-agnostic: it is a one-function change with no call-site churn. Recommended LogSnag, because comparability with v1's existing funnel is what makes the number actionable.
close_reason: Closed

title: Build the presentational Wordle board component
description:
Build the presentational Wordle board component in v2 against the design system.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: this task is the board as a DISPLAY component — given a set of guesses, render
it. The entry interaction (keyboard, mobile viewport-aware sheet, submit handling) is Phase 2
work and stays there. Splitting it this way is deliberate: the board is the design system's
signature component, so it belongs to the system, while entry is core-loop behaviour.

Spec, DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 6: 5-column grid, 6 rows, gap-1 (4px), fixed 320px width on
desktop. Letters uppercase, text-3xl md:text-4xl.

TILES ARE SQUARE — radius 0. The doc is emphatic twice ('Don't round them', 'the sharp corner is
the game's visual signature'). This is the one place the radius vocabulary does not apply.

States read tokens, never inline accents: correct -> --wordle-correct (white-ish text), present
-> --wordle-present paired with --warning-foreground, absent -> --wordle-absent, empty -> no
fill, border only via --wordle-tile-border.

Also port the display rules: 7 attempts renders X, a missed day before today scores 0, non-play
weekends render N/A in muted text, and boards can be hidden per team until the viewing player
has submitted their own for that day.
acceptance_criteria: All four tile states plus X, 0 and N/A render from tokens with square corners in both themes; grep for green-|yellow- utilities in the component returns nothing.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-18.

SHIPPED: src/lib/wordle.ts (pure logic), src/lib/wordle.test.ts (18 tests), src/components/wordle-board.tsx, src/components/score-cell.tsx. vitest.config.ts now also includes src/**/*.test.ts — it was convex-only, so any src test would silently never have run.

Logic was split out of the component so the duplicate-letter rules can be tested without a DOM. That is where the value was: two of my own first-draft test expectations were wrong, and working them out by hand is what surfaced the bug below.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: grid is exactly 320px at md, tiles compute to border-radius 0px, font-size 36px (text-4xl), and the four states resolve to the right tokens in both themes. Score cells render 4 / X / 0 / blank / N-A, covering all five v1 rules.

TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM v1, both contrast:
 1. Tile foregrounds now travel with their background instead of inheriting the page foreground. v1's PRESENT tile inherits, so in DARK mode it is near-white on #eab308 — 1.84:1, below even the 3:1 large-text floor, on the signature component. Pairing it with --warning-foreground gives 9.83:1. This is a live v1 bug that the design system's own token pairing fixes.
 2. CORRECT tiles take --success-foreground (white-ish) per DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 6, rather than inheriting. Worth being honest that this is slightly LOWER contrast than v1 in light mode — 3.30:1 vs v1's inherited 6.00:1 — but tiles are text-3xl/4xl, so the 3:1 large-text threshold applies and it clears. Chose it because the doc explicitly says white-ish text and because an inherited foreground flips colour between themes, which is what styles.css rule 2 warns against. Easy to revert to inherit if you would rather have the higher number.

A REAL v1 BUG FOUND AND FILED, NOT FIXED: wt-ksh.12.10. v1's pass 2 demotes the EARLIER duplicate 'present' rather than the later surplus one, so a legitimate yellow is lost. Answer SPEED, guess GEESE: real Wordle gives -YGY- (two E's shown, matching the answer), v1 and this port give --GY- (one E). The player is told a correct letter is wrong. NOT fixed here because the board is squarely inside the strict-parity scope — A7's exception covers login/onboarding only, and silently changing scoring feedback during a re-skin is exactly the drift the parity rule exists to prevent. Pinned by a deliberately-named test so it cannot change by accident.

SCOPE HELD: presentational only. Entry interaction (keyboard, mobile viewport-aware sheet, submit handling) stays in Phase 2. v1's team-context dependency became showLetters/boardEntry props. v1's padArray MUTATED its input; toRows does not.

INCIDENT WORTH KNOWING: I ran pnpm build from the repo ROOT by mistake, which built v1 (Next.js) and dirtied the tracked public/sw.js and public/sw.js.map — exactly wordle-teams-d9g. Reverted with git checkout; nothing reached a commit. Always confirm pwd is v2/ before pnpm anything.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add the Phase 2 shadcn component set with the documented fixes
description:
Add the shadcn components Phase 2 consumes, with the design system's documented fixes applied.

Set: button, card, badge, table, dialog, sheet, tabs, select, switch, input, skeleton, sonner,
input-otp, avatar, dropdown-menu, separator. Anything beyond this defers to the phase that needs
it. Do NOT bring over aceternity or magicui — border-beam is the only magicui piece
DESIGN_SYSTEM.md references and it is marketing-only decoration.

Fixes to apply while adding, from DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 10 and MIGRATION.md:
 1. Badge `success` variant must be bg-success + text-success-foreground. v1 pairs bg-green-600
    with text-secondary-foreground = ~2.1:1, a live WCAG AA failure. Add a matching `warning`.
 2. Card padding: v1 forked the primitive to px-4 py-6 md:p-6. Pick ONE default and let
    consumers override; do not fork the primitive again.
 3. Radius: bind each component to a single step off --radius. v1 has md, lg, xl and a one-off
    rounded-[6px] at the same hierarchy level.
 4. Toast severity: v1's sonner success and error render identically. Give each an accent edge
    or icon.
 5. Font as a token: font-display vs font-sans, rather than v1's per-element className.

Card titles are text-2xl font-semibold with a right-aligned action row on the same line.
DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 7 calls this deliberate and characteristic, not a mistake. Keep it.
acceptance_criteria: Every listed component renders in both themes on a scratch route; the success badge measures at least 4.5:1 in light mode; no aceternity or magicui dependency was added.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-18 from wt-ksh.12.3 — fix #1 in this task's description is WRONG AS WRITTEN. Do not apply it verbatim.

This task says the Badge success variant 'must be bg-success + text-success-foreground' because v1 pairs bg-green-600 with text-secondary-foreground at '~2.1:1, a live WCAG AA failure'. That came from DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 10. Recomputed against a checker validated on six published WCAG reference pairs: v1's actual pair, near-black #111113 on green-600 #16a34a, is 5.72:1 and PASSES AA. The bundle's prescribed replacement, white on #16a34a, is 3.30:1 and FAILS. v1's badge was never broken.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: bg-success + text-success-foreground is still the right shape — the point stands that the accent should be a token rather than an inline green-600 — but it is a TOKENIZATION change, not a contrast fix, and the win is smaller than advertised. It is now safe on contrast only because wt-ksh.12.3 darkened --success (light) from #16a34a to #15803d, which puts white-on-success at 5.02:1. With the bundle's original value it would have shipped a regression.

Knock-on for this task: there is no live accessibility bug to cite as justification, so if the badge work is ever descoped, nothing is being left broken. Also note --accent-foreground no longer exists as the brand pair; it is --accent-solid-foreground (see wt-ksh.12.3 for why). And v1's success badge behaviour is a legitimate parity target after all.

Separately, wordle-correct light stays #16a34a while success light is now #15803d, so the badge green and the correct-tile green differ slightly in light mode. That is deliberate: tiles carry text-3xl/4xl where 3.30:1 clears the large-text bar, and the tile is the game's colour.
DONE 2026-08-18. All 16 components in, all five fixes resolved — but the style choice from wt-ksh.12.2 had to be reversed, for a real reason.

STYLE CHANGED radix-nova -> default. THE radix-nova REGISTRY VARIANT IS BROKEN UPSTREAM: it imports Radix primitives but styles on BASE UI data attributes. Confirmed by fetching the registry directly — ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/radix-nova/switch.json imports 'radix-ui' yet contains 4 occurrences of data-checked: and zero of data-[state=, identical selectors to base-nova. Radix emits data-state="checked" and data-orientation="horizontal"; Base UI emits data-checked and data-horizontal. Blast radius before the fix: ~80 mismatched selectors across 8 components (dialog, dropdown-menu, select, separator, sheet, switch, tabs, table).

CAUGHT VISUALLY, NOT BY THE TOOLCHAIN. Build, tsc and tests were all green with it broken — Tailwind simply never generated the rules. It showed up in a screenshot as an invisible Switch: the track computed to rgba(0,0,0,0) with a white thumb on a near-white page, and the Separator measured 96x0. This is the argument for the screenshot step being part of the gate, not decoration.

default IS radix-native (data-[state=) and internally consistent, and it is what v1's own components.json uses, so it is also the parity-correct choice. It matches DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 7 metrics out of the box far better than nova did: badge rounded-full px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold, switch 44x24 track with a 20px thumb, solid destructive rather than nova's tinted one. This retires my earlier claim on wt-ksh.12.2 that the New York/Default prompt was 'moot' — it is the legacy axis, but the legacy styles are the ones that actually work with Radix.

THE FIVE FIXES:
 1. Badge success + warning variants added, tokenised (bg-success/text-success-foreground). Measured live in both themes: 5.02:1 light, 4.79:1 dark, both clearing AA. The task's original contrast justification was wrong (see the correction note above); this is a tokenisation change and is documented as such in the component.
 2. Card padding — NO CHANGE NEEDED. Nothing forks the primitive; consumers override normally.
 3. Radius vocabulary — NO CHANGE NEEDED under default. Audited all 16: button/input md, card/dialog lg, badge/avatar/switch full, skeleton md-overridable. That is exactly DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 4, unsurprisingly, since the doc describes v1 and v1 uses this style. Drift #8 was about v1's CONSUMERS, not its primitives.
 4. Toast severity — sonner ships distinct per-severity icon shapes; success and error additionally take their semantic colour (5.02:1 and 4.83:1 on the toast surface). warning and info deliberately inherit: --warning is #facc15 at 1.7:1 there, so colouring it would read as broken. Verified an error toast renders with the red octagon-X.
 5. Font as a token — DONE HERE rather than deferred. Google Fonts import swapped Fraunces+Manrope -> Inter+Geist; --font-sans: Inter and a new --font-display: Geist; the .display-title CSS class deleted in favour of the font-display utility. Verified computed body font is Inter.

A DEFECT I WOULD HAVE INTRODUCED: shadcn's stock sonner.tsx imports useTheme from next-themes, which v2 does not use — it would have been a second theme source of truth disagreeing with ThemeToggle whenever a user picks a mode explicitly. Added src/lib/use-resolved-theme.ts, which reads the authoritative .dark class via MutationObserver, and removed next-themes from the dependency set.

VERIFIED: build, tsc --noEmit, 15/15 tests. A scratch /gallery route rendered all 16 in both themes at 1100px; dialog, sheet and dropdown all mount and Escape-close; two toasts render. Zero Base-UI attribute selectors remain. No aceternity, magicui or framer dependency. Scratch route deleted and the build re-run clean afterwards.
close_reason: Closed

title: Retire the teal sea/lagoon palette from v2
description:
Retire the teal sea/lagoon palette and move the existing v2 surface onto the design system.

Owner decision 2026-08-18: the design system supersedes. It is neutral + green + yellow and
states 'No rebrand... the green->yellow accent stays'; the teal palette is an unrelated identity
that would ship as a rebrand and break parity.

Blast radius, measured 2026-08-18 — this is why the phase is sequenced before Phase 2, and it
only grows from here:
 - v2/src/styles.css: the sea-ink / sea-ink-soft / lagoon / lagoon-deep / palm / sand / foam /
   surface / line / kicker / hero-* token block, in :root, :root[data-theme="dark"] and the
   prefers-color-scheme block, plus 51 hand-rolled classes
 - v2/src/routes/about.tsx, v2/src/routes/index.tsx, v2/src/routes/login.tsx
 - v2/src/components/Header.tsx, Footer.tsx, ThemeToggle.tsx

Prefer replacing hand-rolled classes with shadcn components where one exists (Card, Button,
Separator, Badge) rather than re-pointing the class at a new token.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rE 'sea-ink|lagoon|palm|foam|sand|kicker|hero-[ab]' v2/src returns nothing, and all five routes render correctly in both themes on a phone viewport.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-18.

REMOVED: all three teal token blocks (:root, :root[data-theme=dark], and the prefers-color-scheme block), the starter's layered radial-gradient body background, and 25 unused .demo-* classes. styles.css went 656 -> ~326 lines; compiled CSS 50,890 -> 43,268 bytes.

A LIVE BUG THIS FIXED, not just cleanup. The teal block redefined --surface (and it sat AFTER the design-system :root), so --surface resolved to the translucent #ffffffbd in light. Worse in dark: :root[data-theme=dark] beat .dark on specificity, so --surface was #101e22cc. The design-system surface token was never actually in effect. Verified in the compiled CSS before (5 --surface declarations, teal winning) and after (exactly 2: :root #fff, .dark #121212). wt-ksh.12.3's checks confirmed token presence and utility generation, both true, but did not catch the shadowing.

KEPT, re-expressed in tokens: page-wrap (layout only), display-title, island-kicker (-> text-muted), island-shell (-> surface + border-subtle + the system's shadow-sm, dropping the stacked teal shadows and backdrop blur), nav-link (-> text-muted/text with an accent-solid underline sweep).

COMPONENTS MIGRATED: Header, Footer, ThemeToggle, about.tsx. The teal chip/header/link vars became bg-surface, border-line-subtle, text-foreground, text-muted-foreground, hover:bg-muted; the hardcoded #56c6be->#7ed3bf dot gradient became from-brand-from via-brand-via to-brand-to.

DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED:
 - index.tsx. It is the Phase 1 walking-skeleton debug page, self-described as 'deliberately plain', and its data-testid hooks back the e2e tests. Phase 2 replaces it, so styling it now is throwaway work.
 - login.tsx. Zero colour classes and zero teal, so nothing to retire; it is entirely unstyled and belongs to wt-ksh.12.7.
 - Fonts. Still Manrope + Fraunces from the starter; DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 3 wants Inter + Geist and font-as-token is wt-ksh.12.5 item 5. Noted in-file.
 - TanStack starter CONTENT (wordmark, Docs link, social links, footer copy, /about copy). Content, not colour — filed as wt-ksh.12.9 rather than absorbed.

VERIFIED: build, tsc --noEmit, 15/15 tests. Zero teal identifiers remain in v2/src outside explanatory comments, and sea-ink/lagoon/data-theme/demo-/bg-base/header-bg are all absent from the compiled CSS. Screenshotted /about and /login at 390x844, both themes, via the project's own Playwright chromium: computed body colours are exactly rgb(250,250,250)/rgb(10,10,11) light and rgb(10,10,10)/rgb(250,250,250) dark. The card now reads as a real step off the page in both themes, which is the surface hierarchy the design system adds and which the --surface collision had been suppressing.

NOTE FOR wt-ksh.12.7: no CSS keys off data-theme any more — theming is entirely the .dark class, which ThemeToggle sets in all three modes. The data-theme attribute is now informational only. Also, v2's login already renders VISIBLE TEXT LABELS on all four provider buttons (Google/Microsoft/GitHub/Discord), so v2 never inherited v1's icon-only tooltip grid; that half of wordle-teams-390 is structurally satisfied already and 12.7 is mostly styling plus the funnel events.
close_reason: Closed

title: Translate the v2 token set into v2/src/styles.css as Tailwind v4
description:
Translate the design system's v2 token set into v2/src/styles.css as Tailwind v4.

Source of values: tokens.json -> v2 block. Source of structure: globals.v2.css, which is
Tailwind 3 and cannot be dropped in. Translate, do not copy:
 - @tailwind base/components/utilities  ->  already @import "tailwindcss"
 - @layer base { :root { --token: <bare hsl triplet> } } + hsl(var(--token)) in tailwind.config.ts
   ->  @theme inline with --color-* names
 - .dark class  ->  keep working as-is; v2's ThemeToggle.tsx already adds a light/dark CLASS to
   <html> alongside data-theme, so .dark selectors work unchanged. Preserve the existing

description:
Initialize shadcn/ui inside v2/ so the component set has somewhere to land.

MUST BE RUN FROM INSIDE v2/. Running `shadcn` at the repo root misdetects the project as v1
(Next.js 15.4.10, Tailwind v3, rsc true) and — verified 2026-08-18 — even resolves tailwindCss
to docs/design-system/globals.v2.css, the handoff file we just committed. Initializing from the
root would write config against the wrong app.

Settings: Tailwind v4 (so @theme inline, not tailwind.config.ts), TypeScript, rsc FALSE
(TanStack Start, not RSC), iconLibrary lucide (already a v2 dep), base RADIX to match v1's
component APIs — parity means matching v1's vocabulary, and v1 is Radix-backed.
CLI templates include `start` for TanStack Start. Package manager is pnpm@11.20.0, so
`pnpm dlx shadcn@latest`.
acceptance_criteria: v2/components.json exists and points at v2/src/styles.css; the @/ alias resolves; one added component renders under vite dev and vite build passes.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-18. Verified: vite build passes, tsc --noEmit clean, 15/15 vitest pass, and a Button rendered server-side under vite dev on /about (smoke test reverted afterwards). Compiled CSS confirms the mapping works, not just that it compiled: dist has .bg-primary{background-color:var(--primary)} plus --primary defined in both light and dark, and the existing teal tokens are untouched.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE TASK AS WRITTEN:

1. The alias is #/, NOT @/. v2's tsconfig maps '#/*' -> './src/*' and every existing import uses it. The task's done-when said @/ because I assumed shadcn's default; kept the codebase's convention instead of introducing a second alias. components.json aliases are all #/-prefixed.

2. There is no 'base' field in components.json. The published schema (ui.shadcn.com/schema.json) has required [style, tailwind, rsc, aliases] and NO base property — the base is encoded into style, e.g. 'radix-nova'. Writing base:'radix' produces 'Invalid configuration found'. So the radix-base decision is expressed as style:'radix-nova'. This also means the interactive 'New York vs Default' prompt is the legacy style axis, not the base choice, and my earlier plan to pick 'Default' for v1 parity was moot.

3. shadcn init is INTERACTIVE even with --yes, and its prompts need a real TTY — piped stdin and piped arrow-key escape sequences are both ignored, and a pty via script(1) hung. Bypassed by hand-authoring components.json against the schema, then 'pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add button --yes', which is fully non-interactive and correct. That is the path for wt-ksh.12.5's 16 components.

WHAT init WOULD HAVE DONE THAT I DID BY HAND: created src/lib/utils.ts with cn(); installed class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge, radix-ui, tw-animate-css; added @import 'tw-animate-css', @custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *)), an @theme inline color/radius mapping and a :root/.dark value block to src/styles.css.

title: Phase 1.5 — Design system foundation (import Claude Design system into v2)
description:
Import the design system built in Claude Design (derived from v1, then improved) into v2, and
build the component vocabulary Phase 2 needs, BEFORE Phase 2 builds board entry and scoreboard.

## Why this phase exists, and why here

v2's UI is effectively greenfield: v2/src/components holds three files (Header, Footer,
ThemeToggle), there is no shadcn install and no components.json, and the entire visual system
is a hand-rolled 464-line v2/src/styles.css — the sea/lagoon/palm/sand token set with light,
dark and prefers-color-scheme variants.

Phase 2 is the first phase that builds substantial UI. Landing the design system after Phase 2
means restyling the board and scoreboard; landing it before means building them once. The
window for this being cheap closes when Phase 2 starts.

## What the artifacts are

CSS / Tailwind theme tokens, plus static HTML/CSS mockups. No React components — translating
mockups to TSX is part of the work. As of 2026-08-18 the artifacts are NOT in the repo and not
in ~/Downloads; exporting them out of Claude Design is task one and is an owner action.

## Relationship to the parity rule

Amendment A7 (2026-08-18) added the login/onboarding surface as a third sanctioned exception to
strict-1:1 parity, alongside reactivity and passkeys. This phase is where that exception gets
spent: login/onboarding is the one surface where the design system may change behaviour, not
just appearance, because wordle-teams-390's fix (labeled provider buttons instead of an
icon-only tooltip grid) is design work on the product's largest known leak.

Everywhere else, the design system changes how screens look, not what they do. A3 still governs
which version of v1 behaviour ports.

## Scope boundaries

IN: token import/reconciliation, the component vocabulary Phase 2 consumes, the login/onboarding
surface, light+dark parity, mobile-first verification.

OUT: redesigning screens that do not exist yet (teams, invites, payments, reminders) — those get
built on the system in their own phases, not retrofitted in this one. Out too: any behaviour
change outside login/onboarding.

## Open questions — resolve when the export lands, before the task breakdown is final

1. Do the Claude Design tokens SUPERSEDE the existing styles.css sea/lagoon palette, or extend
   it? Determines whether Header/Footer/ThemeToggle and the existing static pages get restyled.
2. Does v2 adopt shadcn (matching v1's vocabulary: button, card, dialog, drawer, sheet, tabs,
   input-otp, sonner, table...) or stay hand-rolled on Tailwind v4? v1 also pulls aceternity and
   magicui, which are almost certainly not worth carrying over.
3. How much of the mockups' component surface does Phase 2 actually need, versus what defers to
   the phase that consumes it?
4. Dark mode: the existing styles.css supports data-theme plus prefers-color-scheme. Do the
   Claude Design tokens cover dark, or is that ours to derive?

## Done when

The design system's tokens are the single source of truth in v2, every component Phase 2 needs
exists and renders correctly in light and dark on a phone, and the login screen on beta uses
labeled provider buttons rather than the icon-only tooltip grid.
acceptance_criteria: Design system tokens are the single source of truth in v2/src/styles.css; every component Phase 2 needs exists and renders correctly in light and dark on a phone; beta's login screen uses labeled provider buttons instead of the icon-only tooltip grid.
notes:
ARTIFACTS REVIEWED 2026-08-18. All four open questions are now answered, and one finding changes this phase's shape.

THE BUNDLE TARGETS v1, NOT v2. The README says it proposes tokens 'for the v2 replatform', but every concrete artifact is aimed at the existing Next.js app. 'v1 -> v2' in this bundle means token-set version 1 -> version 2, applied in place to main. Evidence:
 - globals.v2.css is described as 'a drop-in replacement for src/app/globals.css' — v1's path — and is Tailwind 3 syntax: @tailwind base/components/utilities, @layer base, @apply border-border, .dark class.
 - tailwind.tokens.ts expects a tailwind.config.ts theme.extend.colors block consuming hsl(var(--token)). v2 has no tailwind.config.ts; it is Tailwind v4 via @tailwindcss/vite with an @theme block.
 - The whole Layer 3 alias block exists so src/components/ui/* compiles unchanged. That is v1's ~30 shadcn components. v2 has three components and no shadcn.
 - MIGRATION.md phases 2-4 name v1 files exclusively: wordle-board.tsx, ui/badge.tsx, app-bar/app-bar-base.tsx, home/feature-cards.tsx, magicui/border-beam.tsx.
 - tokens.json meta: stack 'Next.js + Tailwind + shadcn/ui', themeMechanism '.dark class on <html> via next-themes', branch main, captured 2026-08-03.
DO NOT run MIGRATION.md as written against v2. Use DESIGN_SYSTEM.md sections 1-11 as the spec and tokens.json's v2 block as the value source, translated to Tailwind v4.

WHY THIS IS STILL THE RIGHT INPUT: the bundle is a source-derived capture of v1's design plus a normalization pass. Adopting it in v2 does not violate strict-1:1 parity — it ENCODES parity, minus the nine catalogued drift items. That is a better fit for this project than a fresh design would have been.

Q1 SUPERSEDE OR EXTEND — SUPERSEDE, and this is a real cost. The design system is neutral + green + yellow and states 'No rebrand... the green->yellow accent stays'. v2's current styles.css is an unrelated teal palette (sea-ink, lagoon, palm, sand, foam). They are incompatible; one must win, and it should be the design system, because v1 is what users know and parity is the rule. Blast radius is small NOW and grows: the teal tokens are used by src/routes/about.tsx, Header.tsx, Footer.tsx, ThemeToggle.tsx and 51 hand-rolled classes in styles.css, across 5 routes total. This is the argument for doing the phase before Phase 2, quantified.

Q2 SHADCN OR HAND-ROLLED — ADOPT SHADCN in v2. Three reasons: the bundle's entire compat layer presumes it; v1's component vocabulary IS shadcn and parity means matching it; and Phase 2 needs table, dialog, sheet, tabs, select, switch, input, badge, card, skeleton, toast and input-otp, which is a lot to hand-roll. Do NOT carry over aceternity or magicui — border-beam is the only magicui piece the design doc references and it is marketing-only.

Q3 COMPONENT SURFACE PHASE 2 NEEDS — the Wordle board (signature: 5x6 grid, gap-1, 320px desktop, SQUARE tiles, radius 0), the leaderboard table (pinned Player column left, Score column right, both painted bg-background so rows slide under), dialog-on-desktop / sheet-on-mobile as one content component with two presentations, plus button, card, badge, select, skeleton, toast. Everything else defers to the phase that consumes it.

Q4 DARK MODE — COVERED. tokens.json v2 and globals.v2.css both carry full light+dark, with a verified contrast table in MIGRATION.md. Better than expected: v2's ThemeToggle.tsx already adds a light/dark CLASS to <html> alongside data-theme, so the bundle's .dark selectors work in v2 unchanged.

BUGS THE BUNDLE FIXES THAT v2 MUST NOT INHERIT: the success badge pairs bg-green-600 with text-secondary-foreground, ~2.1:1, fails WCAG AA. Also nine catalogued drift items in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 10.

NOT COVERED BY THE BUNDLE: the A7 login exception. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md documents the OTP input but gives no guidance on the provider-button grid, so wordle-teams-390's labeled-button fix is additive work in this phase, not something the bundle hands us.
PHASE COMPLETE 2026-08-18. All seven planned tasks (wt-ksh.12.2 .. .12.8) closed, plus the .12.1 export.

DONE-WHEN VERIFIED ON BETA, NOT JUST LOCALLY. Six deploy-v2 workflow runs succeeded on feat/v2-replatform; the latest is live. Measured on https://beta.wordleteams.com/login at 390x844 in both themes: body background rgb(250,250,250) light and rgb(10,10,10) dark, body font Inter, a real <h1> 'Sign in', --accent-solid resolving to #15803d light and #22c55e dark (the AA-corrected values from wt-ksh.12.3), and all four provider buttons carrying visible text labels. Zero teal identifiers in the served HTML.

Gate at close: vite build clean, tsc --noEmit clean, 33/33 unit tests, 2/2 e2e.

WHAT CHANGED VERSUS THE PLAN, and why:
 - Style went radix-nova -> default. The radix-nova registry variant is broken upstream (Radix imports, Base UI selectors). default is radix-native and is what v1 uses, so it is also the parity-correct answer.
 - Fonts were done here rather than deferred, since the base layer was already being rewritten.
 - Fixes 2 and 3 (card padding, radius vocabulary) turned out to be no-ops under default — nothing forks the primitive and the radii already match DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 4.

FOUR DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED that the bundle did not flag: the --surface collision that meant the design-system surface token was never in effect; the --accent-foreground double-declaration; shadcn CardTitle rendering a plain div so a Card-wrapped page has no h1; and sonner importing next-themes as a second theme source of truth.

THE BUNDLE'S CONTRAST TABLE IS UNRELIABLE and its headline badge fix is inverted — v1's pair is 5.72:1 and passes, the prescribed replacement is 3.30:1 and fails. Four token values deviate deliberately as a result. All of this is written up in docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md.

THREE ISSUES REMAIN OPEN under this phase, none blocking Phase 2:
 - wt-ksh.12.11 (P1, owner): funnel events have no destination, so wordle-teams-390 still cannot be attributed. Recommended LogSnag.
 - wt-ksh.12.9 (P2): header/footer/about still carry TanStack starter content. Must not reach cutover.
 - wt-ksh.12.10 (P2): v1 board over-demotes duplicate letters; reproduced faithfully and pinned by test, to be fixed deliberately.

Phase 2 (wt-ksh.3) is now unblocked and will be built on the design system rather than restyled afterwards, which was the whole point of sequencing this phase here.
