title: dev.yaml and prod.yaml still install the Supabase CLI with version: latest
description:
Gap in my own wt-465 fix. I pinned .github/workflows/ci.yaml and did not check the other two workflows using the same action:

  ci.yaml    version: 2.114.0   (pinned by wt-465)
  dev.yaml   version: latest
  prod.yaml  version: latest

prod.yaml is the one that matters. It runs on push to main and does:
  supabase link --project-ref $SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID
  supabase db push --include-all
against the PRODUCTION database, then syncs Novu state. So the tool applying migrations to production is whatever Supabase released most recently, chosen at run time and never reviewed.

That is a strictly worse exposure than the one wt-465 fixed. There, an unexpected CLI version turned a types check red — noisy but harmless, and obvious. Here it changes the behaviour of a migration push against prod, where the failure mode is quiet and not obviously attributable to a version bump. 2.114.0 shipping on 2026-08-12 already changed enough to break the types check; nobody reviewed what else changed.

dev.yaml has the same shape against the dev database, which is lower stakes but the same argument.

Low risk on the release currently open (PR #163): git diff origin/main..origin/dev -- supabase/ is empty, so there are no new migrations and db push --include-all has nothing to apply. This matters for the first release that DOES carry a migration.

Pin both to the same version ci.yaml uses, so a CLI bump is one deliberate PR across all three rather than three independent moving targets.
acceptance_criteria: All three workflows install a pinned Supabase CLI version, and bumping it is a single reviewable change.

title: CI 'Verify generated types are checked in' fails on every PR: setup-cli uses version: latest
description:
.github/workflows/ci.yaml:14-28 installs the Supabase CLI with 'version: latest', runs 'supabase start', regenerates src/lib/database.types.ts and fails if it differs from the committed file.

Because the CLI is unpinned, the local stack it starts — including Supabase's INTERNAL storage schema — moves whenever Supabase ships a release. When it moves, the regenerated file no longer matches what is committed and the check fails on every PR until someone regenerates. That is a time bomb, not a code check: the same commit passes one week and fails the next with no change to the repo.

It has now gone off. PR #157 fails this step. Verified it is unrelated to that PR's contents: regenerating locally produces 226 changed lines across 48 hunks, and ALL 48 are inside the storage schema section. Zero are inside the public schema (lines 35-344 and the public Constants block at 979-983 in the committed file). Examples: enum buckettype gains VECTOR, storage function params renamed to p_bucket_id / p_sort_order / p_start_after, storage.buckets gains deleted_at and name.

dev last ran green on 2026-08-03. Nothing has merged since, so the drift is entirely upstream.

Note that simply regenerating and committing does NOT reliably fix it: the file has to match whatever version CI resolves at run time. Regenerating with the local CLI (2.110.0) is a guess unless it happens to equal CI's 'latest' at that moment. Pinning is what makes the check meaningful.

Suggested: pin setup-cli to an explicit version, regenerate once against that version, and commit both together. Then bumping the CLI becomes a deliberate PR with a reviewable types diff, which is what this check was presumably meant to enforce. Optionally narrow generation to the schemas the app uses (--schema public) so Supabase-internal churn cannot break the build at all.
acceptance_criteria: A PR that changes no database schema passes the types check regardless of when it runs, and bumping the Supabase CLI produces a reviewable diff in src/lib/database.types.ts rather than a red check on unrelated work.
notes:
FIXED on fix/pin-supabase-cli, PR #158 into dev, CI green. Not yet merged.

Two commits, because pinning alone was NOT enough:
  be305e9  setup-cli version: latest -> 2.114.0, with a comment on why
  9887e0b  regenerate database.types.ts against that version

The first CI run after pinning still failed: the committed types did not match a fresh 2.114.0 stack either, so the drift predates 2.114.0 and the file had to be regenerated regardless.

THE REGENERATED FILE CAME FROM CI, NOT LOCALLY, and that distinction matters for next time. 'supabase gen types --local' reads whatever stack is ALREADY RUNNING. This machine's stack was built by an older CLI (local 2.110.0, and the containers older still), so regenerating here produces a plausible file that still does not match a fresh install of the pinned version. The workflow prints the exact 'git diff' on failure — extract that from the run log, strip the 'test\t<step>\t' prefix, the ISO timestamp and the ANSI codes, and it applies cleanly with git apply.

Verified before committing:
  all 48 changed hunks inside Supabase's internal storage schema
  public schema byte-identical — 0 changed lines in its type block (35-344) or its Constants block (979-983)
  nothing in src/ references Database["storage"] or graphql_public
  pnpm build compiles
  the same workflow still FAILS on the commit before the regeneration, so the check is still doing its job rather than defanged

MERGE ORDER: #158 before #157. #157 then needs a rebase or a re-run to pick up the pinned config.

WATCH OUT — the beads pre-commit hook exported the whole tracker into what should have been a two-file CI change, adding 62 lines of unrelated churn and setting up a conflict with #157, which edits .beads/issues.jsonl from a different base. Removed with 'git checkout origin/dev -- .beads/issues.jsonl' plus 'git commit --no-verify'. Anything branching off dev for a non-beads change will hit this.

STILL OPEN AS A CHOICE, not done: the app only uses the public schema, so 'supabase gen types typescript --local --schema public' would make this check permanently immune to Supabase-internal churn and shrink the committed file a lot. Pinning stops unrelated PRs breaking; --schema public stops the file churning at all. Deliberately left out of #158.

title: handleLogsnagEvent awaits logsnag.track() with no try/catch, so a LogSnag outage blocks sign-in
description:
src/lib/utils.ts:301-329. On a first sign-in, handleLogsnagEvent does 'await logsnag.track({...})' with no error handling. finishSignIn awaits handleLogsnagEvent (utils.ts:249), and the auth callback route awaits finishSignIn inside a try/catch whose only behaviour is to redirect to /login-error (api/auth/callback/route.ts:38-43).

So if LogSnag is down, rate-limits, or the token is rejected, a user whose credentials verified perfectly gets sent to /login-error. The session cookies may already be set at that point, leaving the user in a confusing half-state: authenticated but told sign-in failed.

Compare createNovuSubscriber immediately below it (utils.ts:255-269), which wraps its network call in try/catch and only logs — that is the right shape. handleLogsnagEvent is the odd one out. Note 'new Novu(process.env.NOVU_API_KEY!)' at utils.ts:258 is also OUTSIDE its try block, so a constructor throw there has the same effect.

Analytics must not be able to fail a login. Wrap both in try/catch and log, matching createNovuSubscriber.

Found while building a local repro harness for wt-uc5: the callback route kept redirecting to /login-error and this was one of two candidate causes. The actual cause there turned out to be a prod/local Supabase mismatch, so this path was NOT observed failing in production — it is a code-reading finding, not an incident. Filing it because the blast radius is 'nobody can log in' and the fix is four lines.
acceptance_criteria: LogSnag or Novu failing (bad token, network error, non-2xx) does not prevent a successful sign-in from reaching /me. Verify by pointing LOGSNAG_TOKEN at an invalid value locally and confirming the callback still lands on /me.
notes:
FIXED on fix/logsnag-blocks-signin. Both analytics calls in finishSignIn's path are now non-throwing, matching notifyBilling in lib/polar/notify.ts, which already had this property and the reasoning written down.

THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN DOES NOT REPRODUCE THE BUG. It said 'point LOGSNAG_TOKEN at an invalid value'. Probing the SDK directly:
  invalid token string -> NO THROW, track() returns true (LogSnag accepts any bearer token)
  undefined token      -> NO THROW, returns true
  EMPTY string token   -> THROWS HTTPResponseError
The first run of the acceptance test passed against UNFIXED code for exactly this reason. What actually throws is any non-2xx — logsnag/dist/client/logsnag.js:95 and four sibling call sites raise HTTPResponseError on every one — which is what an outage, a rate limit or a 5xx produces. An empty token reproduces it reliably and is itself a realistic misconfiguration: an env var that exists but failed to populate.

CONFIRMED REAL, differential against the running app (next dev, local Supabase, fresh user each run so isFirstSignIn is true and the LogSnag branch actually executes):
  unfixed, LOGSNAG_TOKEN='' -> /login-error?token_hash=...  (a valid sign-in rejected)
  fixed,   LOGSNAG_TOKEN='' -> /me
So this was NOT merely a code-reading finding, as the description assumed. A LogSnag non-2xx does fail a real sign-in.

THE NOVU HALF IS ALSO A GENUINE INSTANCE, not defensive tidying. new Novu(undefined) and new Novu('') both throw 'Missing secret key'; only a garbage-but-present key constructs. The constructor sat outside its own try block (utils.ts:258), so an unset or blank NOVU_API_KEY failed sign-in the same way. Two independent env-var misconfigurations could each take down all sign-ins.

BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN THE DESCRIPTION SAYS: finishSignIn has TWO callers, the OAuth callback route AND verifyOtp in login/actions.ts:144. Email OTP sign-in was equally exposed, not just OAuth.

Dropped both to log.warn. A missed analytics event is a degraded non-essential path, not an application error, and error-level noise on ordinary flows is the same problem 3io fixed.

Harness: verify_4ov.sh in the session scratchpad. It mints a fresh user via admin.generateLink so no SMTP is needed, and matches on the redirect PATH because the callback carries the original query string through to /login-error.

title: OTP verify submits with an empty token on the prod login form
description:
Observed in production on 2026-08-10 during a real new-user signup (the only email-provider signup since the 2026-08-03 release).

Axiom, prod, level=error:
  22:55:55.858  'Signups not allowed for otp'
  22:56:06.291  'Verify requires either a token or a token hash'

The second error comes from supabase.auth.verifyOtp() in src/app/login/actions.ts:107 being called with an empty/missing 'otp' field. The user had to POST /login four times over 33 seconds before getting in (22:55:53, 22:56:01, 22:56:06, 22:56:26). Only the fourth succeeded.

The form in src/app/login/email/otp.tsx submits to the verifyOtp server action without guarding that a token is present, so a submit that lands before the code is entered (or before hydration attaches the handler) reaches the server as a tokenless verify and burns an attempt with a generic 'Verification failed. Please try again.'

Note: the v2 branch (9f7ea15) hardens an equivalent flow, but that is the Better Auth/Convex stack. Production still runs the Supabase path, so v2 does not fix this for current users.
acceptance_criteria: verifyOtp rejects a missing/empty token client-side before the server action fires, and the login form is inert until hydrated. No further 'Verify requires either a token or a token hash' events in the prod Axiom dataset.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-14 on fix/signup-activation (e3089bc), NOT yet deployed.

Root cause was simpler than the issue description assumed. The description floated a pre-hydration submit as a possible path; that is not it. <Otp /> is only mounted after the parent's effect reads the awaitingVerification cookie (login/page.tsx:14), so the OTP form never renders before hydration. The real cause is that nothing stopped a click on an empty form: OtpSchema was declared at otp.tsx:15 and never called, and unlike login-form.tsx (which gets native 'required' on its email Input) a custom OTP component has no browser-level guard. The 5-second gap between the code being requested and the failed verify fits an impatient click, not a hydration race.

Changes:
  - otpSchema moved to email/schemas.ts beside loginSchema/signupSchema
  - otp.tsx: code is controlled state, email read via useEffect, submit disabled until both present
  - actions.ts verifyOtp: validates before calling Supabase, returns the specific message

Disabling the button (rather than guarding inside onClick) is load-bearing: a disabled default button also suppresses implicit submission from Enter in the code field, which the differential test showed was a second live path.

VERIFICATION — differential, against the running form:
  unfixed code: empty form fires 2 server-action POSTs, button enabled at 0 and 3 digits
  fixed code:   empty form fires 0 POSTs, button disabled at 0/3 digits and without an email cookie, enabled at 6
  pnpm lint: no new warnings (10 pre-existing elsewhere, none in src/app/login)
  pnpm build: passes

The harness is Python Playwright and is NOT in the repo — the repo has no test framework and adding one was explicitly out of scope. It lives in the session scratchpad as verify_otp_guard.py. To rebuild it: set cookies awaitingVerification=true and email=<anything> on localhost:3000, load /login, and assert the Submit button's disabled state plus the count of POSTs to /login. Supabase is not needed; the OTP step is reached by cookie alone.

STILL OPEN: this stops the bad request being sent. It does not address why the user was on the verification step with nothing to enter — see 3io for the login/signup split that put them there.

title: P1.T8: Phase 1 verification & close-out
description:
Full local gate (unit, typecheck, build, e2e), the phase done-when on beta, prod regression sanity, then close wt-ksh.2.

DONE-WHEN, per the design minus passkeys: a real COPIED account logs in on beta via OTP and via Google, and lands on a page showing its own copied data.

The design's criterion also said 'and enrols a passkey'. Passkeys were deferred to post-cutover on 2026-08-11 — they are one of only two sanctioned NEW features in the replatform, and a new feature on the phase that gates every other phase is the wrong trade while @convex-dev/better-auth is still pre-1.0.
acceptance_criteria: Done-when met on beta, local gate green, prod unaffected, wt-ksh.2 closed.
notes:
2026-08-18 local gate GREEN on feat/v2-replatform @ the copied-data commit:
  typecheck  tsc --noEmit clean
  unit       15/15 pass
  build      vite build ok, routeTree.gen.ts untouched, Register block intact
  e2e        2/2 pass

E2E NEEDED A LOCAL-BACKEND FIX FIRST, worth recording: a convex dev process had been running 5 days with a dead file watcher, so the local anonymous deployment never received me.ts and the signed-in page died with 'Could not find public function for me:myData'. Killing pid and re-running 'convex dev --once' fixed it. If e2e fails with a missing-function error, suspect a stale local backend before suspecting the code.

GAP FOUND AND CLOSED: the done-when says the account must land on 'a page showing its own copied data', and the landing page showed only the email plus the Phase 0 status message — a copied account was indistinguishable from a new one, so the criterion was NOT actually verifiable. Added convex/me.ts (me:myData) and rendered it. e2e now asserts the panel renders, because writing it broke the signed-in page and the existing assertions caught that only incidentally.

PROD REGRESSION SANITY: PASS. git diff 0dc6cfd..HEAD touches only v2/, scripts/, docs/, .beads/. No v1 application source changed. The two new scripts/ files are read-only prod diagnostics with the prod-ref guard, printing counts only.

BETA VERIFIED (signed-out, real browser): / redirects to /login; all four provider buttons render; copied-data panel does NOT leak to signed-out users.

REMAINING FOR CLOSE-OUT — needs the owner, since it requires signing in:
confirm that on beta a COPIED account shows ITS OWN teams and board-entry count in the new 'Your copied data' panel, via OTP and via Google. Everything else in T8 is done.
close_reason: Local gate green (typecheck, 15 unit, build, 2 e2e). Prod regression sanity pass — no v1 source touched. Done-when MET on beta, confirmed by owner: a copied account logs in via OTP and via Google and sees its own teams and board-entry count in the new 'Your copied data' panel.

title: P1.T6: copy-from-supabase script, scoped and re-runnable
description:
v2/scripts/copy-from-supabase.ts: read Supabase with the service-role key, write through Convex internal mutations, idempotent on legacyId, and take a SCOPE argument.

SCOPE DECISION (owner, 2026-08-11): copy only the owner's teams and their players for now, not all 530 users. beta.wordleteams.com is publicly reachable with no auth wall and Phases 2-6 are months of work; putting every user's email and name there that early is not worth it. The full copy runs at the Phase 7 parity audit and again in the cutover window. Write the script for the full set from day one so Phase 7 changes an argument, not the code.

MUST: lowercase every invited[] entry as it writes (see P1.T1). Create Better Auth users by email with the verified flag, so P1.T5's account linking has something to link to. Read-only against Supabase. Never print addresses — this repo is public. Follow the existing scripts/*.mjs conventions, which already carry a prod-ref guard.

Depends on P1.T1.
acceptance_criteria: Running it twice produces identical row counts, and the owner's account exists in Convex with its real teams and scores.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-12. Copy is live against the beta deployment and idempotent: a second run is 0 inserts, 7130 updates, identical counts.

IN CONVEX NOW (owner's teams only, per the scope decision): 18 players, 6 teams, 6948 dailyScores, 61 monthlyWinners, 18 playerMembership, 79 webhookEvents. Counts match Supabase exactly for the scoped set.

THREE THINGS CHANGED DURING THE BUILD, ALL FROM EVIDENCE RATHER THAN REVIEW:

1. KEYING. The first version upserted daily scores on player+date, on the stated premise that it is the pair the app treats as unique. False: v1 has no such constraint and upsertBoard INSERTs whenever the client has no scoreId, so double submits create duplicates. Production holds 5. The old key silently collapsed them, which would have made the Phase 7 parity check report an unexplainable difference. Now keyed on legacyId like every other table; duplicates filed as wordle-teams-rac and deliberately NOT repaired inside a migration.

2. date IS NOT A CALENDAR DAY. The schema said 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Supabase types it timestamptz and v1 stores whatever the client sends; the production time-of-day histogram is a broad spread peaking at 12-13:00Z, not a normalised midnight.

3. puzzleDay ADDED, fixing the owner's cross-timezone report. See the v1 bug issue for the full analysis. Backfilled in each player's own timezone; 544 of the 6948 scoped rows land on a different day than a naive UTC read.

OPERATIONAL NOTES FOR THE PHASE 7 AND CUTOVER RE-RUNS:
  Needs CONVEX_MIGRATION_KEY (runInternalMutations + runInternalQueries), NOT the everyday deploy key.
  purgeCopiedData exists for a clean re-copy and is batched — Convex caps an execution at 4096 reads and the scoped set alone is ~7000 rows. It deletes children before parents.
  Changing a field's validator on a populated table needs a widen-purge-narrow dance; the copy shape is settled now, so this should not recur.
  Script is .mjs rather than the plan's .ts: v2 has no tsx and the repo's other prod scripts are .mjs.
close_reason: Copy live and idempotent against beta: 18 players, 6 teams, 6948 daily scores and the rest, counts matching Supabase for the scoped set, second run producing zero inserts. Also delivered the puzzleDay fix for the cross-timezone bug the owner reported.

title: P1.T5: Four social providers + account linking by verified email
description:
Wire google, azure, github and discord in createAuth (v2/convex/auth.ts), with account linking by VERIFIED email so a copied account reached via Google resolves to the same user as via OTP.

Account linking on a verified email is the mechanism that makes the whole migration survivable: copied users are created by email, and a social login must land on that same user rather than minting a second one.

AMENDED 2026-08-17: was five providers. X/Twitter dropped — see wordle-teams-aw3. The 2 X users both hold confirmed emails and fall back to OTP on the same address, verified by scripts/prod-twitter-users-fallback.mjs. Slack was already dropped (zero users).

WATCH: expectAuth:true blocks ALL Convex queries for signed-out users. The provider buttons live on /login, which is signed-out. If a provider button ever needs live Convex data it will hang.

FOUR REGISTRATIONS IS FOUR CHANCES TO MISCONFIGURE A CALLBACK. Test each provider individually on beta — a working Google says nothing about Discord.

Callback shape: https://beta.wordleteams.com/api/auth/callback/<providerId>, served by the TanStack route src/routes/api/auth/$.ts at SITE_URL — NOT the Convex site domain.

Depends on P1.T4 for credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Signing in with each of the five providers on beta succeeds, and Google on a copied account lands on the SAME user as OTP on that address rather than creating a second one.
notes:
2026-08-18 (5): MICROSOFT PERSONAL ACCOUNT SIGN-IN WORKS. The mapProfileToUser emailVerified fix resolved account_not_linked. Full path exercised: authorize -> callback -> claim evaluation -> account linking.

WORK-ACCOUNT 'approval required' IS NOT A DEFECT — measured, not assumed. Owner's work tenant is 98825390-a76d-41dd-8297-5f60fc12f17b. Prod has ZERO azure users from that tenant, so v1 never held consent there either. That directory is being asked to consent to this app for the FIRST time and requires an admin to do it; v1 would have hit the identical wall. Dropping the 'profile' scope would NOT help, because the gate is app-level consent, not the scope delta.

=> The owner's work account is the one account guaranteed to need approval, so it cannot be used to validate Microsoft. Recommend treating microsoft as VERIFIED on the strength of the personal-account run; the work/school path differs only in which endpoint issues the token, and the 15 real users already use this same app registration successfully under v1.

DECIDED: keep the 'profile' scope. Considered dropping it to match v1's consent surface exactly, since the 12 tenants that DO have users consented only to email+offline_access+openid and 'profile' can trigger incremental consent. Rejected: profile is 'Admin consent required: No', so those users self-consent as they already did for v1, and losing display names for every Microsoft user to hedge a hypothetical is the worse trade.

CARRY TO PHASE 8 (wt-ksh.8 / cutover): any of the 12 tenants that disables user consent will prompt its users for admin approval at cutover and need that org's own admin. Unfixable from the app. Not anticipated in the original plan.
close_reason: All four providers sign in successfully on beta: google, microsoft (personal, incl. the emailVerified fix), github, discord. Google verified on a COPIED account resolving to the same user as OTP — the account-linking criterion. Two real fixes came out of it: User.Read removed, and mapProfileToUser deciding emailVerified.

title: P1.T1: Convex schema for the six tables
description:
Define players, teams, dailyScores, monthlyWinners, playerMembership and webhookEvents with the indexes later phases need, legacyId on every table for idempotent re-copying, and the three corrections in section 4 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-11-v2-phase1-auth-and-data-copy.md.

THREE THINGS THE DESIGN GETS WRONG BECAUSE IT PREDATES THE POLAR MIGRATION AND THE INVITE FIXES:
  1. player_customer is SMALLER than the design assumed. The Polar migration dropped customer_id and membership_variant. Carry membership_status and the player link, nothing else.
  2. webhookId is a STRING, not a uuid. Standard Webhooks ids look like msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W. v1 lost a day to a uuid column that rejected them and put Polar into an infinite retry loop. Convex has no unique constraints, so idempotency goes in the mutation: index on webhookId, look up, return early if present.
  3. invited[] is stored LOWERCASE. v1 matched it case-sensitively while auth lowercased addresses, so mixed-case invitees never joined. A faithful port reproduces the bug. The flow is Phase 4; the storage rule belongs here.
acceptance_criteria: convex deploy pushes the schema clean and pnpm test:once covers insert/read for each of the six tables.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-11. Schema live on the beta/prod Convex deployment (fabulous-goldfish-949) via CI run 31526665092 — all 11 indexes added, no destructive changes. 14 tests cover insert/read for every table.

THE THREE CORRECTIONS ARE IN AND TEST-GUARDED:
  playerMembership carries only legacyId, playerId and membershipStatus. A test asserts customerId and membershipVariant stay ABSENT, so a future 'restore parity with the old schema' cannot quietly reintroduce columns the Polar migration deliberately dropped.
  webhookId is v.optional(v.string()) with a by_webhookId index. A test inserts the literal Standard Webhooks example id, and a second test deliberately writes a DUPLICATE to document that Convex has no unique constraint — the replay guard has to be code in Phase 5's handler, and the index exists to make that lookup cheap.
  invited[] is documented and tested as lowercase-only.

DESIGN CHOICES WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE NEXT PHASES:
  Timestamps are epoch ms, EXCEPT dailyScores.date which stays a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string. A calendar day is not an instant; converting it would invent a timezone the original never had. Phase 2's monthly-winner logic depends on that distinction.
  createdAt is stored separately from Convex's _creationTime, because for copied rows _creationTime is when the copy ran, not when the thing happened. Any 'joined on' or 'first played' display must use createdAt.
  NO INDEX FOR 'teams containing player X'. Convex cannot index array membership. Production has 171 teams total, so collect-and-filter is fine; revisit only if that changes by an order of magnitude. Phase 3 should not invent a join table without measuring first.
  teams.creator is optional so a scoped copy can reference a creator who is outside the scope.
close_reason: Six tables with legacyId and 11 indexes deployed to the beta Convex deployment via CI; 14 tests cover insert/read for each, including guards for all three corrections the design predated.

title: Server-side errors never reach Sentry in v2 — only the client SDK captures
description:
Proven on beta 2026-08-03 while running Phase 0 Step 6 item 4 (wt-ksh.1.12). Two temporary routes were deployed, triggered and removed.

WHAT WORKS: the client. A throw in a React event handler produced pageerror in a real Chromium session, the browser POSTed an envelope carrying an event payload to o177762.ingest.us.sentry.io/api/4511848703918080/envelope/, and it rendered as issue WORDLE-TEAMS-V2-2. @sentry/tanstackstart-react on the client is correctly wired, including the browser-tracing integration.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK: everything server-side. Two different server throws were tried and NEITHER produced a Sentry event:
  1. A route loader throw (/sentry-check?server=true) — TanStack Router caught it, rendered its error page and returned 404.
  2. A server handler throw (/api/sentry-check, the same shape as the working auth route) — also 404, also no event.

DIAGNOSIS: TanStack Start converts errors into RESPONSES before they ever leave the fetch handler. src/server.ts wraps the handler with wrapFetchWithSentry and Sentry.withSentry, but both only see what propagates OUT of the handler, and nothing does — hence 404s rather than 500s. The worker SDK is otherwise alive: every SSR document carries sentry-trace and baggage meta tags keyed to the right project, so init and instrumentation are fine. It is specifically ERROR CAPTURE that is missing.

WHY THIS MATTERS: any exception in a loader, a server function or an API handler is currently invisible in production. The app would return a 404 and Sentry would show nothing. For a replatform whose whole observability story is 'Sentry from Phase 0', that is a hole in the floor — and it is exactly the kind of thing that looks fine until an incident.

NO AUTOMATIC FIX EXISTS IN THIS SDK VERSION. @sentry/tanstackstart-react 10.66.0 exports only captureException and wrapFetchWithSentry on the server side — there is no router-error integration to switch on. So the wiring has to be explicit:
  - a root errorComponent / defaultErrorComponent on the router that calls Sentry.captureException
  - explicit try/catch -> captureException in server handlers, or a shared wrapper for them
  - re-verify BOTH paths afterwards, the same way this was proven, since a 404 with no event looks identical to success

The v2 design already calls for this — 'TanStack Router error boundaries per route section + root boundary -> Sentry' — it simply was never built. Phase 0 wired the SDKs; nobody had yet thrown anything at them.

REPRODUCTION: the two temporary routes are in git history at 84ecb5f and were removed in the commit after.
acceptance_criteria: A thrown error in a route loader AND in a server handler each produce an issue in the wordle-teams-v2 Sentry project, verified by triggering them against a deployed build rather than locally.
notes:
FIXED AND VERIFIED ON BETA 2026-08-03. Three capture paths, each proven against the real deployment rather than locally:

  WORDLE-TEAMS-V2-2  client render/event error        -> already worked
  WORDLE-TEAMS-V2-3  server route handler             -> fixed by withErrorCapture
  WORDLE-TEAMS-V2-4  SSR loader error                 -> fixed by defaultOnCatch

WHAT THE FIX IS:
  src/lib/sentry-capture.ts  isomorphic captureError via @sentry/core. Neither SDK works in both environments — @sentry/tanstackstart-react's SERVER entry exports only wrapFetchWithSentry and has no captureException, and importing @sentry/cloudflare would pull worker-only code into the client bundle. @sentry/core reports through whichever client is bound to the current scope. Pinned exact so it cannot drift from the SDKs.
  src/router.tsx             defaultOnCatch on the router.
  src/lib/server-handler.ts  withErrorCapture wrapper, applied to /api/auth/$.

TWO THINGS LEARNED THE HARD WAY, BOTH COST A DEPLOY CYCLE:

1. A root-route onCatch is DEAD CODE for child routes. TanStack catches at the boundary of the route that threw, not at the root. The diagnostic build produced no log line at all until it moved to defaultOnCatch at the router level.

2. REACT DOES NOT RUN componentDidCatch WHILE SERVER RENDERING. TanStack's CatchBoundary therefore only catches once the client hydrates. This is the actual shape of the coverage and it is not what the issue originally assumed:
   - a real visitor hitting an SSR loader error IS reported, on hydration. Confirmed with a scripted Chromium session: the browser posted an event carrying the SERVER-side message, and it became WORDLE-TEAMS-V2-4.
   - the SAME request from curl or a crawler, which never hydrates, is NOT reported. Narrow and understood: user-facing errors always involve a browser.
   - server route handlers are unaffected and report with no browser at all, which is why the wrapper matters independently.
   That limit is documented next to defaultOnCatch in src/router.tsx so it is not rediscovered.

The startInstance registration and the Sentry global middlewares in src/start.ts were present and correct all along — worth noting, since wt-ksh.1.15's route-tree drift was a plausible suspect and was NOT the cause.

FOUR TEST ISSUES IN SENTRY ARE SAFE TO RESOLVE: WORDLE-TEAMS-V2-1 through -4.

VERIFICATION GOTCHA: the Sentry issues API defaults to an is:unresolved filter that hides issues and briefly made it look like nothing had ever landed. Always pass an explicit empty query= parameter.
close_reason: Server-side error capture implemented and verified end to end on beta. Route errors report via defaultOnCatch at the router level, server handlers via a withErrorCapture wrapper, both through an isomorphic @sentry/core capture helper. Proven with real triggered errors: WORDLE-TEAMS-V2-3 (handler, no browser involved) and -4 (SSR loader, on hydration). One documented limit remains by design: an SSR loader error on a request that never hydrates — curl, crawlers — is not reported.

title: DECISION: the v2 cost driver no longer survives contact with the funnel data
description:
The v2 design's first stated driver is cost: 'Vercel pricing grows steeply with scale; Cloudflare's curve is much flatter. Get ahead of growth.' Two measurements taken AFTER that design was approved describe a product with no growth to get ahead of.

ACTIVATION (wordle-teams-456, prod 2026-07-30): 526 players exist; 68 have ever entered a board with guesses. 458 accounts — 87% — signed up and never played once. Of the 68, 50 are outside the owner's teams and 40 of those entered one or two boards and stopped. Exactly one independent team ever sustained multi-user use, and it churned in May 2025. Current volume is 3-7 board entries a day, essentially all from the owner's six teams.

LOGIN CONVERSION (wordle-teams-390, 30d to 2026-07-30): ~163 real people reached /login; roughly 12 completed an auth round-trip. Zero server-side auth failures in the window.

The design's own constraint line reads '~40 DAU in production daily'. Measured independent DAU is close to zero.

TWO CAVEATS BEFORE OVER-READING THIS. The login number probably has a mechanical cause that is now fixed: /login was completely unusable for anyone blocking app.lemonsqueezy.com — an infinite client-side error loop, 998 errors in 500ms, invisible in server logs (wordle-teams-jvt). Lemon Squeezy is now gone from the codebase entirely, so the funnel needs re-measuring before 7% means anything. And some unmeasured share of the 458 zero-score accounts are invite-flow casualties from a bug that is now fixed.

THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT TO CANCEL v2. DX/architecture fit and vendor reduction (~10 -> ~6) are unaffected by traffic, and a solo developer's productivity on a preferred stack is a legitimate driver on its own.

WHAT IT DOES MEAN: demote cost from lead driver to secondary benefit, and treat sequencing as open rather than settled. A strict-1:1 parity rewrite faithfully reproduces a funnel that activates 13% of signups; finishing Phases 1-9 and THEN discovering the product problem is the risk. Options: (a) re-measure the funnel now that jvt and the invite bug are fixed, before committing further; (b) interleave funnel work with the port; (c) proceed as planned on the DX driver alone.

See amendment A5 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md.
acceptance_criteria: Owner has picked one of (a), (b) or (c) and the epic wt-ksh reflects it.
notes: Owner decision, not agent work. Depends on nothing; blocks nothing mechanically, but the answer changes how much of wt-ksh is worth doing and in what order.
close_reason: Owner chose (b) interleave funnel work with the port, 2026-08-18. Recorded as amendment A7 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md and in the notes on epic wt-ksh. Cost demoted to secondary driver; login/onboarding added as a third sanctioned parity exception; funnel instrumentation is now a v2 deliverable. New phase wt-ksh.12 inserted before Phase 2.

title: Verify the PRODUCTION invite email template was ever updated in the Supabase dashboard
description:
supabase/config.toml:72-75 configures a custom invite template (supabase/templates/invite.html) and states plainly that it applies to LOCAL only: 'The PROD equivalent must be set in the Supabase dashboard (Authentication -> Email Templates -> Invite user).' Nothing in the repo or in any issue confirms that was actually done.

WHY IT MATTERS. The custom template routes the invitee straight to the app:
    {{ .SiteURL }}/api/auth/callback?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=invite&next=/me
That path is proven to work — scripts/validate-invite-dev.mjs verifies token_hash -> verifyOtp -> handle_invited_signup end to end.

Supabase's DEFAULT invite template instead renders {{ .ConfirmationURL }}, which routes through /auth/v1/verify with redirect_to taken from the redirectTo passed to inviteUserByEmail. Until PR #156 that value was scheme-less, and a scheme-less redirect_to is silently discarded in favour of the Site URL (proven by scripts/verify-auth-redirect-allowlist.mjs). The invitee would land on the bare homepage, where nothing exchanges the token, and would never join the team.

That is precisely the symptom epic wordle-teams-c0v set out to fix and never confirmed fixed. So this is the leading explanation for why invites appeared broken after that epic shipped.

HOW TO CHECK: Supabase dashboard -> project 'Wordle Teams' (dcfqzbdusxhrfgvnpwqc) -> Authentication -> Email Templates -> 'Invite user'. Confirm it matches supabase/templates/invite.html. Check the Dev project (sgrxuealmksermhjqepj) too.

Could not be checked from the CLI: no management token is available, and 'supabase config' exposes only 'push', which is a write against the linked project and would apply the whole local config.toml.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: the production invite email template is confirmed to match supabase/templates/invite.html, or is updated to match, and the same is confirmed for the Dev project.
close_reason: Owner confirmed 2026-08-03: the production invite email template IS the custom one matching supabase/templates/invite.html, and the invite flow is verified working. So prod routes invitees through {{ .SiteURL }}/api/auth/callback with token_hash, never through /auth/v1/verify, and the scheme-less redirectTo was never reached. The Dev project's template was not separately checked, but it is low stakes — dev invites are exercised via scripts/validate-invite-dev.mjs against token_hash directly.

title: Downgrade the paying customer if they have not moved to Polar by 2026-09-05
description:
After the Polar cutover, NOTHING revokes membership_status any more. Verified in production 2026-08-03: cancelling a Lemon Squeezy subscription at period end fires subscription_cancelled, which reaches https://wordleteams.com/api/webhook and is rejected 403, because that route now validates Polar Standard Webhooks signatures and a Lemon Squeezy payload carries an X-Signature HMAC instead. webhook_events did not move (403 happens before any DB write). subscription_expired at period end will hit the same wall.

So the grace period granted to the paying customer (player b447fded-dff1-4911-8c9c-23535a8031ad, LS customer 7242020) is UNBOUNDED unless someone ends it by hand. Cancelling at period end stops the billing; it does not stop the access.

Their Lemon Squeezy period ends 2026-08-05. The migration email offers a free first period on Polar, so roughly a month of grace after that is consistent with what they were promised.

ON 2026-09-05, CHECK: has player b447fded got an active Polar subscription?
  - YES  -> nothing to do. Polar owns their lifecycle from then on and subscription.revoked will downgrade them correctly and automatically.
  - NO   -> set player_customer.membership_status for b447fded to 'expired' and run handle_downgrade_team_removal for them, mirroring what the webhook would have done. Consider a reminder email first.

title: auth-urls.ts builds invite links from VERCEL_URL, which has no scheme when deployed
description:
src/lib/auth-urls.ts does:

  const base = process.env.VERCEL_URL ? `${process.env.VERCEL_URL}/api/auth/callback` : 'http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback'

VERCEL_URL is NOT a project-defined variable (confirmed via 'vercel env ls'). It is Vercel's SYSTEM variable, whose value is the bare deployment hostname with no scheme — 'wordle-teams-abc123-....vercel.app'. Only .env.local overrides it, where it is set to 'http://localhost:3000'. So the file's comment claiming VERCEL_URL 'is set to a full canonical URL in this project's environment' holds locally and nowhere else.

Consequences if unfixed: invite emails would carry a redirectTo with no scheme, and a deployment-specific hostname that sits behind deployment protection rather than the canonical domain. Supabase would likely reject it against the redirect allowlist and fall back to the Site URL — which is EXACTLY the original failure mode the invite epic (wordle-teams-c0v) set out to fix.

NOT YET CONFIRMED to be broken in practice — that epic's acceptance criterion (an invitee clicking through and landing authenticated) was never verified by a real invitee click; its notes still list 'Pending: invitee clicks'. So the invite fix may never have actually worked in production, for this reason.

Discovered while fixing the identical flaw in the Polar module, where it DID break: appOrigin() built success_url the same way, Polar rejected it with 422 'Input should be a valid URL', and every checkout on dev failed. See wordle-teams-8sg.

Fix is the same shape: canonical domains keyed off ENVIRONMENT, as src/lib/polar/client.ts appOrigin() now does.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: authCallbackUrl returns an absolute URL on the canonical domain in every environment, and a real invite link is clicked through end to end on dev.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-03. Owner confirmed the production invite template is the custom one and that the invite flow is verified working.

FINAL ASSESSMENT: ev8 was a real code defect with NO live impact. Neither email flow ever rendered the bad value:
  * login — dashboard template sends a 6-digit code with no link, so emailRedirectTo is never used. Owner verified the OTP flow works.
  * invite — the custom template builds its link from {{ .SiteURL }} and hardcodes next=/me, ignoring the redirectTo passed to inviteUserByEmail. Confirmed present in production and working.

So my earlier claims that this was 'confirmed broken in production' and that it explained wordle-teams-390 were both wrong. I verified Supabase's redirect behaviour but not whether either template reached it. wordle-teams-390 is unexplained again and needs its own investigation — the login funnel is entirely OTP-code based, so the drop-off is somewhere in that flow, not in a link.

WHAT THE FIX IS WORTH ANYWAY: authCallbackUrl no longer returns a scheme-less, deployment-specific URL, so it is correct if a template is ever switched to {{ .ConfirmationURL }} — at which point the old code would have failed silently, exactly as it does for anything routed through /auth/v1/verify. The Polar and auth copies of the origin ternary are now one function, so the mistake that DID break Polar checkout cannot recur in a third copy. scripts/verify-auth-redirect-allowlist.mjs makes the allowlist checkable, read-only, in seconds.

Merged in PR #156; production deploy Ready.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #156 (merged, prod deploy Ready). authCallbackUrl now returns an absolute URL on the canonical domain in every environment, via a canonicalOrigin() shared with the Polar module. The second acceptance criterion — a real invite click-through — is moot: the invite template builds its link from {{ .SiteURL }} and never uses this value, and the owner has confirmed the prod template is the custom one and the invite flow works. Defect was real but had no live impact; see notes for the corrected analysis.

title: Polar P3: verification script and dev verification
description:
No test framework exists, so this follows the established scripts/*.mjs pattern.

CREATE scripts/verify-polar-sandbox.mjs - creates a checkout and a portal session by external_customer_id, asserts both return usable URLs.

VERIFY ON DEV: (1) Exercise mapEventToTransition over every Polar event name - pure, so no network or DB needed. (2) Complete a sandbox checkout with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 against dev; assert the webhook_events row, the player_customer transition, and the RPC's effect on teams. (3) LOGIN REGRESSION - highest stakes, because of the auth hook rewrite. Per the standing note, dev.wordleteams.com is behind Vercel SSO so curl cannot reach it; this must go through supabase-js against dev Supabase the way scripts/validate-invite-dev.mjs already does. (4) Confirm subscription.canceled alone does NOT downgrade - the single most important behavioral difference from the LS integration.

notes:
VERIFIED END TO END 2026-08-03. The redelivery closed the loop. webhook_events : subscription.active, player cfb26858-..., processed=true, no error player_customer: cfb26858-... -> pro Polar delivery : http 202 (original, silently did nothing) -> http 200 (redelivery) customer.external_id : null -> cfb26858-... (self-heal fired) The redelivery exercised the FALLBACK path specifically, which is what makes it valuable: that customer still had external_id null and the original checkout carried no metadata, so the only route to the player id was subscription.checkoutId -> checkout.external_customer_id. The new code is therefore proven against real Polar, not just against stubs. The repair also means every future event for this customer arrives with customer.externalId populated and takes the fast path with no API call. FULL DEV VERIFICATION NOW COMPLETE: - auth hook / login after the migration: 14/14 against dev Supabase - Polar sandbox API: 13/13 live, incl. a regression guard on scheme-less success_url - portal.ts against real Polar: returns no-customer correctly (422 + detail, not 404) - offline suites: 6 files, ~120 assertions - real checkout -> payment -> webhook -> membership: PASSES Three real bugs were caught by dev verification that no amount of offline testing would have found: appOrigin building success_url from VERCEL_URL (every checkout failed), the portal's 404 check that could never match (Polar sends 422), and customer.external_id being null for pre-existing customers (silent 202, nobody upgraded). The last one would have hit production hardest, since polar-migrate imports customers. Spec corrected. Remaining owner-side item, tracked here rather than blocking: both Polar product descriptions contain literal HTML that renders as visible

tags on the checkout page — needs fixing in sandbox and production.

title: Polar P2d: rewrite webhook route for Polar
description:
Rewrite src/app/api/webhook/route.ts. Path stays /api/webhook (one provider, still accurate).

FLOW: (1) validateEvent(rawBody, headers, secret) from @polar-sh/sdk/webhooks; on WebhookVerificationError return 403. (2) playerId = event.data.customer.external_id. (3) If missing or not a UUID, log and return 202 NOT 500 - webhook_events.player_id is NOT NULL with an FK to players, so a foreign event would fail the insert and make Polar retry forever on something that can never succeed. (4) webhookId from the 'webhook-id' HEADER - Polar follows Standard Webhooks, so unlike LS's meta.webhook_id it is not in the body. Column is already text, no type change. (5) Store event; on unique-index conflict it is an already-handled retry, return 200. (6) Apply transition from P2b, run the RPC, mark processed.

Also delete src/lib/typeguards.ts outright - validateEvent returns discriminated typed events, so webhookHasMeta/webhookHasData have nothing left to guard. Update processWebhookEvent/storeWebhookEvent in src/app/me/actions.ts:292-397 accordingly, including deleting the per-webhook getFreeVariantId() API call.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a valid sandbox event updates player_customer and runs the right RPC; an invalid signature returns 403; a replayed webhook-id returns 200 without reprocessing; an event with an unknown external_id returns 202.
notes:
CORRECTION from j8c: the issue description says webhook_id is 'already text, no type change'. That was WRONG — the column was uuid (Lemon Squeezy's meta.webhook_id happened to be one, and database.types.ts renders uuid as string, which hid it). Migration 20260731120000 now converts it to text, verified locally. Standard Webhooks does not require UUIDs; the spec's own example id is msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W. Do NOT assume the header value parses as a UUID.

ALSO FROM j8c: gen-types moved OUT of j8c and into ymy. Regenerating database.types.ts breaks typecheck in utils.ts:107-108, me/page.tsx:41, and app-bar-server.tsx:31-33, and fixing those is ymy's type-ripple scope. j8c therefore shipped SQL only, keeping the repo green.

The unique index is PARTIAL (where webhook_id is not null), so legacy rows with a null webhook_id are exempt. A duplicate non-null webhook_id raises a unique violation on insert — catch that specifically and return 200, since it means an already-handled retry.
close_reason: Webhook route rewritten for Polar; also closed the server-action escalation path, proven via the build manifest

title: Polar P2c: checkout and portal modules
description:
Create src/lib/polar/checkout.ts with createProCheckout(playerId, email, name) -> checkout URL, and src/lib/polar/portal.ts with getCustomerPortalUrl(playerId).

Checkout uses POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID directly (replacing the current listProducts + .find(p => p.attributes.name === 'Pro') name lookup, deleting an API round-trip per checkout and a fragile string match). Sets external_customer_id = playerId, prefills customer email/name, and sets success_url to /me?checkout=success on the environment-appropriate origin (the existing url ternary in src/lib/lemonsqueezy/index.ts:14-20 has the right shape).

Portal creates a customer session via external_customer_id rather than a stored Polar customer UUID - this is what lets player_customer.customer_id be dropped entirely. Portal URLs are short-lived, so always generate fresh at click time, never store.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: both functions return usable URLs against Polar sandbox, and the portal path never reads a customer id from the database.
notes:
Done. src/lib/polar/checkout.ts (createProCheckout) and src/lib/polar/portal.ts (getCustomerPortalUrl). client.ts gained proProductIds() returning [annual, monthly] and appOrigin(); POLAR_PRO_PRODUCT_ID replaced by the monthly/annual pair.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: portal.ts first matched a missing customer with 'error instanceof ResourceNotFound'. That check can NEVER match. The SDK only raises its typed error classes for responses declared in the OpenAPI spec, and customerSessions.create does not declare a 404 — it throws the generic SDKError. Probing the SDK with a stubbed 404 confirmed: 'THREW SDKError', not ResourceNotFound. Shipped as written, every player who had never checked out would have been told to try again later, forever, for a condition retrying can never fix. Now matched on 'error instanceof PolarError && error.statusCode === 404'. PolarError is the base of both classes and carries statusCode, so it holds whichever a future SDK version throws.

getCustomerPortalUrl returns a discriminated PortalResult ({url} | {url:null,reason:'no-customer'} | {url:null,reason:'error'}) so ymy's UI can say something true instead of a generic retry message. no-customer logs at info, not error — it is an expected state, not a fault.

appOrigin() follows the VERCEL_URL convention from src/lib/auth-urls.ts rather than the hardcoded ENVIRONMENT ternary the Lemon Squeezy module used. Noted in a comment as worth consolidating with auth-urls.ts if a third caller appears.

Verified: tsc clean, pnpm build exits 0, pnpm lint adds no warnings, and 22 assertions pass by intercepting fetch — asserting the exact request body Polar receives (both products, annual first, external_customer_id, no customer UUID, success_url, return_url), every failure branch, the log levels, and that neither module imports supabase. Live URL round-trip deferred to P3 (8sg), which has been updated.

title: Polar P2b: pure event-mapping module
description:
Create src/lib/polar/events.ts with mapEventToTransition(eventType) -> { status, rpc } | null. Pure function, no I/O, no Supabase, no network - it holds the only real logic in the integration and is the unit most worth verifying independently.

MAPPING (see epic for why cancel != revoke):
  subscription.active     -> pro,     rpc: upgrade
  subscription.uncanceled -> pro,     rpc: upgrade (no-op if already pro)
  subscription.canceled   -> null     (NO CHANGE - access paid through period end)
  subscription.past_due   -> null     (NO CHANGE - recoverable)
  subscription.revoked    -> expired, rpc: downgrade

revoked maps to 'expired' unconditionally; distinguishing 'cancelled' would cost a payload branch and nothing reads the difference - only 'pro' gates anything.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: every one of the five subscribed event names returns the mapping above, and an unknown event name returns null rather than throwing.
notes:
Done. src/lib/polar/events.ts exports mapEventToTransition(eventType), ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS, and the MembershipTransition / MembershipRpc types. rpc values are the literal Postgres function names (handle_upgrade_team_invites / handle_downgrade_team_removal) so P2d has no indirection to resolve.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: the first implementation used Record<string, ...>, whose lookup walks the prototype chain. mapEventToTransition('toString') returned Object.prototype.toString (a Function) and '__proto__' returned {} — both truthy, both violating the documented 'unknown yields null' contract, and both would have reached P2d as a truthy transition with an undefined status, producing a database write of undefined membership_status. Not exploitable, since event types arrive inside signature-validated Polar payloads, but the contract was wrong. Switched to a Map, which has no prototype chain. Also froze the shared GRANT/REVOKE objects: both grant events return the same object, so an unfrozen result let a caller mutating one silently corrupt the other.

CROSS-CHECK WORTH REPEATING IN P2D: the verification reads the 37 event-type string literals straight out of @polar-sh/sdk's payload .d.ts files and asserts every acknowledged name exists among them. This specifically guards the British 'subscription.cancelled' typo, which is easy to write here because the app's own member_status enum uses 'cancelled' while Polar's event is 'subscription.canceled'.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, pnpm build exits 0, pnpm lint adds no warnings, and 26 assertions pass covering the five mapped events, seven unknown names, four prototype keys, the SDK cross-check, ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENTS contents, and the freeze behavior.
close_reason: Event mapping landed and verified; 26 assertions pass, prototype-chain bug found and fixed during verification

tags on the checkout page.

title: EPIC: Migrate billing from Lemon Squeezy to Polar.sh
description:
Full spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-polar-migration-design.md. Owner runbook for dashboard setup: docs/plans/2026-07-31-polar-phase1-setup.md. Branch: feat/polar-migration.

WHY NOW: Polar cannot import active subscriptions from Lemon Squeezy (polar-migrate moves products/customers/discounts only). Every paying customer must re-subscribe by hand, so the cost scales with subscriber count and is at its minimum at one paying customer.

KEY DECISIONS: (1) Hard cutover, LS removed entirely in one release. (2) No Polar Free product; 'free' is a DB default, never webhook-driven. (3) external_customer_id = player_id, so Polar customer UUID is never stored, which lets player_customer.customer_id AND membership_variant both be DROPPED rather than retyped int->uuid. (4) Downgrade on subscription.revoked ONLY, never on subscription.canceled, because Polar splits cancel-scheduled from access-ended and a literal port would strip a paying customer's teams weeks early. (5) Hosted redirect checkout, no third-party script, which also removes the DNS-filter failure mode lemon.js has. (6) Customer email held until dev is verified so cutover is a deploy, not a project.

OUT OF SCOPE: polar-migrate tooling; the three Postgres RPCs (handle_upgrade_team_invites, handle_downgrade_team_removal, handle_free_team_limit) which branch on membership_status='pro' and stay untouched by design; the two untracked scripts/*-dev.mjs files in the working tree.

HIGHEST RISK: the migration must 'create or replace' custom_access_token_hook BEFORE dropping player_customer.customer_id and membership_variant, in the same file. Dropping first makes the hook throw and breaks EVERY login. This project already has a login-lockout incident in its history.
acceptance_criteria: 1. New user completes Polar checkout and lands on /me as pro without manual refresh. 2. subscription.revoked downgrades player and removes teams beyond free limit. 3. subscription.canceled alone does NOT change membership_status or remove teams. 4. Existing pro user can open Polar customer portal from user dropdown. 5. Login works after auth hook migration, verified on dev before prod. 6. No Lemon Squeezy reference remains in codebase or Vercel env vars. 7. Duplicate webhook deliveries are idempotent (repeated webhook-id returns 200 without reprocessing).
notes:
POST-CUTOVER BEHAVIOUR CONFIRMED 2026-08-03. Nothing revokes membership_status any more.

Lemon Squeezy webhooks can no longer be processed: /api/webhook validates Polar Standard Webhooks signatures, and an LS payload carries X-Signature instead, so every delivery is rejected 403 before touching the database. Demonstrated in production — 18 rejected deliveries in 33 seconds after an at-period-end cancellation, with webhook_events unchanged at 136 rows.

This is intended for the grace period and means no subscriber loses access during the switch. The corollary is that the grace period has no automatic end, so the paying customer must be downgraded by hand if they never convert; tracked in wordle-teams-g3k, deferred to 2026-09-05. Once a subscriber is on Polar, their lifecycle is automatic again.

Also note the two owner-controlled accounts now sit at 'pro' permanently and free. Deliberate, but it means 'pro' in the database no longer implies a paying subscriber — read it with care.
close_reason: All 11 child tasks complete and Polar is live in production. Acceptance criteria 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 verified (event mapping, auth hook rewrite 14/14 against prod Supabase, no Lemon Squeezy in code or Vercel env, webhook idempotency). Criteria 1 and 4 verified against the Polar sandbox API but not yet with a real production payment, because there are no Polar subscribers — tracked in wordle-teams-7xl rather than left implicit. Remaining Lemon Squeezy store closure is deferred in wordle-teams-0sl; manual downgrade of the unconverted customer is deferred in wordle-teams-g3k.

title: Hydration error + streaming-reveal crash on /me in production (muted in Sentry, 9 users)
description:
Two Sentry issues on the board page that are almost certainly one root cause. Both are PRODUCTION (vercel-production, https://wordleteams.com/me), not dev:

  6804715751  'Hydration Error'                            449 events,  9 users, status IGNORED, last 2026-07-27
  7103187406  TypeError: null is not an object (b.parentNode)  312 events, 2 users, last 2026-07-12

9 users is the second-highest user count in the whole project, behind only the login lockout (wordle-teams-jvt). The sampled events are Mobile Safari / iPhone (iOS 18.7).

The b.parentNode stack is 'app:///me:2 in $RS'. $RS is React's inline streaming-reveal helper (completeBoundary), which moves content out of a hidden template div into a resolved Suspense slot. A null parentNode means the target node was already detached when the boundary resolved — the classic downstream symptom of a hydration mismatch causing React to discard and re-render server HTML. Same page, same environment, same platform as the hydration error, so treat them as one bug until proven otherwise.

WHY THIS WAS MISSED: issue 6804715751 is set to IGNORED in Sentry, so it does not appear in any 'is:unresolved' query — which is how the 2026-07-30 triage pass enumerated issues. It only surfaced when the issues endpoint was queried with an empty status filter. Muted issues need a periodic explicit sweep.

Note the sibling issue 6809975309 ('Cannot read properties of null (parentNode)', 1070 events) is NOT this bug — its events are vercel-preview / dev.wordleteams.com, i.e. dev noise. Do not spend time on it.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce on iOS Safari against production /me and identify the hydration mismatch (likely a date/locale/timezone-dependent render, a Math.random or Date.now in render, or a client-only value used during SSR — the board is date-driven, so suspect date formatting first). Fix the mismatch, then un-ignore 6804715751 in Sentry and confirm the event rate drops to zero.
notes:
FILTER APPLIED 2026-08-17 (2c088d4 on fix/signup-activation), NOT yet deployed.

Chose to drop the event rather than change behaviour, because nothing user-visible is broken and the cost was purely a buried signal. src/lib/sentry-filters.ts holds the predicate — extracted from sentry.client.config.ts so it can be exercised without initialising Sentry and without a DSN, which also means no test traffic reaches the real project.

The predicate requires BOTH a React bootstrap frame (function $RS/$RC/$RX/$RB, or a document-only frame matching ^app:///[^/]*:\d+$) AND a message containing 'parentNode'. Matching on the substring rather than a full string is deliberate: V8 says "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'parentNode')", JavaScriptCore "null is not an object (evaluating 'b.parentNode')", Firefox "b.parentNode is null".

Verified with 10 cases against real event shapes, all passing. The negative cases are the ones that matter:
  KEPT: a genuine parentNode TypeError from a bundle frame (app:///_next/static/chunks/...)
  KEPT: the Hydration Error, which is not a TypeError — wt-dyp depends on it still reporting
  KEPT: an unrelated TypeError even from an $RS-named frame
  KEPT: events with no exception, and message-only events
Also confirmed the filter is actually in the shipped client bundle (its DOCUMENT_FRAME regex appears in main-app), since resolving '@/lib/...' from a root-level config file was the one real risk.
pnpm lint clean, pnpm build passes.

KNOWN TRADE-OFF: replaysOnErrorSampleRate is 1.0, so these errors were reliably pulling in a session replay for /me — which is exactly how this was diagnosed. Dropping the event removes that trigger. replaysSessionSampleRate stays at 0.1, so /me replays keep arriving, just fewer. If wt-dyp needs more of them, raise the session rate temporarily rather than reverting this.

HOW TO VERIFY AFTER DEPLOY: do NOT use issue lastSeen or event counts — error events are being dropped upstream of us (replays report count_errors 0 and the referenced events 404), which is what made this look dormant since 2026-07-27. Instead confirm both halves:
  1. No new events on 6809975309 with a release at or after this deploy.
  2. Production /me replays with op 'navigation.back_forward' STILL appear, proving the trigger still occurs and we suppressed reporting rather than accidentally suppressing traffic.
Read replays with: SENTRY_READ_TOKEN=$SENTRY_WRITE_TOKEN node scripts/sentry-query.mjs raw "projects/christian-white/wordle-teams/replays/<id>/recording-segments/?download=true"

REMAINS OPEN under this issue: nothing. The hydration mismatch and the double document load moved to wt-dyp. Close uc5 once the two checks above hold.

title: PII: real user emails are committed to the PUBLIC repo in .beads/issues.jsonl
description:
github.com/cdub615/wordle-teams is PUBLIC (confirmed via gh repo view). .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked, so every issue body is published. Real user email addresses and first names were reaching that file, including a school-domain address and a corporate one.

DECISION 2026-07-30 (owner): scrub forward only. Existing git history is left as-is — no rewrite, no force-push. The owner's own address in the beads 'owner' field is intentionally retained; only third-party user data is removed.

DONE: all third-party emails and names in the beads DB replaced with stable pseudonyms (invitee-1..invitee-7, owner-alt-account) at redacted.invalid, so distinct people stay distinguishable without being identifiable. One-off prod remediation scripts that hardcode addresses are gitignored via scripts/*-prod.mjs.

STILL TRUE: the pre-scrub addresses remain reachable in published git history and may be indexed or mirrored. Anyone who needs them for debugging should read them from the prod DB, never from the repo.
acceptance_criteria: Adopt the convention that issue bodies reference users by player id, team id, or pseudonym — never by email or real name. Add a pre-commit hook that fails when an email pattern other than the owner's appears in .beads/issues.jsonl or docs/, so this cannot regress.
notes: Scrub script kept at scratchpad/scrub-pii.mjs (dry-run by default). A full pre-scrub backup bundle of all refs is at scratchpad/backup/wordle-teams-pre-scrub.bundle in case any redaction needs reversing. Remaining follow-up: the pre-commit hook is not yet written.
close_reason: Closed

title: Login conversion: 163 human visitors reached /login in 30d, ~7% completed auth
description:
Axiom prod funnel, 2026-06-30..2026-07-30 (30d, the full retention window):

 /login GET 163 unique non-bot IPs, 317 hits
 /login POST 4 unique IPs, 9 requests <- login/signup server action submissions
 /api/auth/callback 8 unique IPs, 14 requests (12 OAuth 'code', 1 invite token_hash, 1 provider error)

So ~163 real people reached the sign-in screen and roughly 12 completed an auth round-trip. Crucially there are ZERO server-side auth failures in the window: no 'Failed to verify OTP', no 'Failed to exchange code for session', no 'Failed to sign in', no 5xx anywhere. The auth backend works. All 6 OAuth providers were verified live against prod Supabase (google, twitter, azure, github, slack, discord) — every one 302s correctly to its provider. People are abandoning at the login screen, not hitting errors.

The email path is nearly unused: only 4 IPs ever submitted the email form in 30 days, and 12 of 14 callbacks were OAuth codes. src/app/login/page.tsx:32 shows OAuthSignin first — a 3x2 grid of six icon-only buttons whose labels exist only as sr-only text plus a hover Tooltip (src/app/login/oauth/oauth-provider.tsx:50-67). Tooltips do not appear on tap, and the heaviest login-page traffic is iPhone (105 hits / 22 IPs). Unlabeled icons on mobile is the leading hypothesis for the abandonment, but the logs cannot prove intent — this needs instrumentation, not more log reading.
acceptance_criteria: Add client-side funnel events for login-page view, provider-button click, and callback arrival so abandonment can be attributed. Then test labeled provider buttons (visible text, not tooltip-only) against the current icon grid and measure completion rate.
notes:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-17. Axiom, production, last 30d (2026-07-18..08-17), bots filtered on user agent:
  /login GET             981 hits, 203 unique IPs
  /login POST             34 hits,   6 unique IPs
  /api/auth/callback      56 hits,  16 unique IPs
Against the original window (2026-06-30..07-30): GET 317 hits/163 IPs, POST 9/4, callback 14/8.

Traffic is up — 163 to 203 people reaching the sign-in screen — and conversion is not: roughly 16 of 203 complete an auth round-trip, about 8% against the original ~7%. The leak is unchanged.

THIS IS STILL A PRE-FIX BASELINE. origin/main is f476605, the 2026-08-03 release, so production has NONE of the 2026-08-14..17 work. wt-odh (OTP form could submit with no code), wt-3io (a first-time visitor on the default Log In tab was told they had failed) and wt-4ov are merged into dev only. Re-measure after a dev -> main release before drawing conclusions about whether they moved anything.

CAVEATS on the numbers, so they are not over-read: unique IP is a rough proxy for people — mobile networks rotate addresses and households share one — so 203 is not 203 individuals. The bot filter is a user-agent heuristic and differs from whatever the original measurement used, so the two windows are not perfectly comparable. Callback hits mix OAuth code exchanges with invite token_hash links.

The original finding still stands and is the important one: there are no server-side auth failures in the window. People are leaving the sign-in screen without hitting an error, which makes this friction and trust rather than a bug — and it is a bigger leak than activation (93% here versus 87% at 456).

title: Middleware never ran in production — root-level middleware.ts is ignored when using src/
description:
CORRECTED 2026-07-30. This issue was originally filed as 'middleware runs on every request incl. static assets, causing 2.4s cold starts'. That premise was WRONG. Middleware was not running at all.

ROOT CAUSE: this project uses a src/ directory, so Next resolves middleware at src/middleware.ts. A root-level middleware.ts is silently ignored — no warning, no build error. Proof:
  - the production build emitted "middleware": {} in .next/server/middleware-manifest.json, with no middleware bundle on disk and sortedMiddleware: []
  - against live prod, a signed-out GET https://wordleteams.com/me returned 200 with no redirect (it should 307 to /login)
  - moving the file to src/middleware.ts immediately produced 'ƒ Middleware 132 kB' in the build and the correct matcher list

WHAT WAS SILENTLY BROKEN THE WHOLE TIME:
  1. Maintenance mode. Flipping maintenance_prod in Edge Config did nothing; the rewrite never executed. Never tested, because it never worked.
  2. The welcome-path redirect (signed-in user on / or /login -> /me). The comment in src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:5-7 says this is specifically what keeps an installed PWA from opening on the welcome screen — so that bug is live for PWA users.
  3. Auth cookie refresh on every request. Plausible contributor to the forced logouts in wordle-teams-io0: without middleware refreshing the session, tokens age out and users get 'Invalid Refresh Token'.

NOT a security hole: every protected page does its own server-side check (src/app/me/page.tsx:31 redirects when !hasSession), so the middleware redirect was belt-and-braces, not the only gate.

THE ORIGINAL PERFORMANCE CLAIM IS UNEXPLAINED. /home 2421ms, /privacy 2258ms, /terms 2159ms, robots.txt 911ms are real measurements, but middleware cannot be the cause. The lambda invocations on robots.txt / sitemap.xml / manifest.json are their own route handlers (src/app/robots.ts, sitemap.ts, manifest.ts). For /privacy and /terms the likely explanation is a cold Next server handling a CDN miss on a prerendered page. That needs a separate investigation — see the follow-up issue.
acceptance_criteria: Middleware executes in production: a signed-out request to /me returns 307 to /login, and toggling maintenance_prod in Edge Config actually serves the maintenance page. Marketing and legal pages and static assets produce no middleware invocation. Neither an Edge Config outage nor a Supabase outage can 500 a matched route.
notes: Fixed on branch fix/middleware-cold-starts. The move is paired with two deliberate changes: (a) the matcher is now an allowlist of /, /login, /me, /branding, /complete-profile rather than a near-catch-all, so enabling middleware does not add invocations to marketing pages; (b) both halves fail open in try/catch, because this is middleware's production debut and every page behind it self-protects. Verified locally: matched routes 307 correctly, unmatched routes untouched, zero errors.
close_reason: Shipped to production 2026-07-30 (main c36d4b1, via dev da0c11d). Verified live: signed-out GET /me, /branding, /complete-profile now 307 to /login — previously 200 with no redirect because middleware never ran. Unmatched routes (/, /login, /home, /privacy, /terms, /about, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, manifest.json) all 200 and untouched. Login page re-verified in a real browser with lemon.js both allowed and blocked: still PASS, so no regression to wordle-teams-jvt. Maintenance mode and the PWA welcome redirect are now functional for the first time — neither has ever been exercised in prod, so watch for surprises. The original 2.2s cold-start claim was misdiagnosed and is split out to its own issue.

title: Activation funnel: 87% of prod signups never enter a single board
description:
Prod data (2026-07-30, scripts/prod-activity-report.mjs): 526 players and 171 teams exist, but only 68 players have ever written a daily_scores row with non-empty guesses. 458 accounts (87%) signed up and never entered one board.

Of the 68 who did enter, 50 are outside Christian's teams and 40 of those 50 entered only 1-2 boards ever, then stopped. Only one independent team ever showed sustained multi-user usage: team 55 (5 players, 39-92 entries each, churned 2025-05-02). Current daily volume is 3-7 entries/day, essentially all from Christian's 6 teams.

This is the same population affected by the invite->join bug (epic wordle-teams-c0v): invitees who could not join the inviter's team would appear as a player row with zero scores, which is exactly this signature. Need to determine what share of the 458 zero-score accounts are invite-flow casualties vs. ordinary signup churn before concluding the invite fix addresses it.
acceptance_criteria: Bucket the 458 zero-score players by origin (invited vs. self-signup) and by whether they ever landed in a team's player_ids. Report what share is attributable to the invite bug fixed in 15d1edb vs. other causes.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-17 to a claim I added when superseding wordle-teams-acf into this issue: I said a zero-team signup lands on /me with 'no board to enter and no obvious next step'. THAT IS WRONG. me/page.tsx:44 does branch to <Intro /> when a user has no team, but src/app/me/intro.tsx renders the full About page with a welcome heading AND a prominent 'Create a Team' button wired to the CreateTeam dialog. There is a clear primary action. I inferred a dead end from the branch without reading what it renders.

So the zero-team screen is NOT the activation blocker I claimed. Whatever is losing the 458 accounts, it is not an absence of a call to action on that screen. This issue's own lead — the invite->join flow, epic c0v — is still the better one, and it is now the leading hypothesis rather than one of two.

title: Nameless just-joined invitee crashes team render (fromDbPlayer throws) + broken complete-profile gate
description:
Exposed by the now-working invite flow (wordle-teams-c0v). When an invitee accepts, handle_invited_signup adds them to teams.player_ids immediately, but first_name is null until they complete their profile.

Bug 1 (gate no-op): src/app/me/utils.ts:18 'if (!hasName(supabase))' is not awaited -> always false -> getTeams returns hasName:true always -> page.tsx:32 never redirects nameless users to /complete-profile.
Bug 2 (crash): src/lib/types.ts:138-139 fromDbPlayer throws on null first/last name; getTeams includes all player_ids members incl. the profile-incomplete invitee -> client TeamsProvider crash rendering the team. Hits invitee AND teammates viewing during the window.

Evidence (dev sgrx): team 43 'Test' player_ids includes 25eeb807 (owner-alt-account@redacted.invalid) with first_name=null; invited[] empty (invite join succeeded).

Fix: (1) await/derive hasName in getTeams so incomplete-profile users route to /complete-profile; (2) filter profile-incomplete players out of each team's rendered players in getTeams (reappear after they complete profile), so teammates don't crash.
acceptance_criteria: Invitee clicking invite link is routed to complete-profile, sets name, then sees the team; a teammate viewing a team with a not-yet-completed invitee does not crash.
close_reason: Fixed: getTeams filters profile-incomplete players + awaits name gate; app/page.tsx awaits hasName. Validated against dev team 43.

title: Invited teammates land on empty state and can only create a team, not join inviter's team
description:
Reported by user invitee-6@redacted.invalid: created team team 206, invited people; when invitees click the email link they can only create a new team instead of seeing team 206 and entering their Wordle board.

Invite/join path (v1 app, dev branch):
- invitePlayer (src/app/me/actions.ts): for new email -> supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail(email,{data:{invited:true}}) + appends email to teams.invited[].
- Invitee clicks link -> /api/auth/callback -> finishSignIn (src/lib/utils.ts) -> handleInvite gates on user.user_metadata.invited===true -> rpc handle_invited_signup(invited_email,invited_id).
- handle_invited_signup (migration 20240517174331) appends invited_id to player_ids for teams WHERE invited_email = ANY(invited), removes from invited, sets user_metadata.invited=false.

Leading hypotheses (need DB/Sentry evidence to confirm):
- B: invitee authenticated via OAuth (Google) instead of clicking the emailed invite link, so the account they use lacks invited:true metadata -> handleInvite never runs.
- E: email case/whitespace mismatch between teams.invited[] entry and auth user email -> WHERE invited_email = ANY(invited) matches nothing.
- A: invitee already had an account -> inviteUserByEmail path differs.

Next: read-only prod query of teams.invited/player_ids for team 206 + auth.users metadata/providers for invitees; check Sentry for handle_invited_signup errors.
design:
Proposed fix (route invite through the callback via token_hash path the app already supports):
1. Pass redirectTo to both inviteUserByEmail calls: `/api/auth/callback?next=/me`.
2. Update Supabase INVITE email template (prod dashboard) to: {{ .SiteURL }}/api/auth/callback?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=invite&next=/me (uses handleEmailSignin/verifyOtp token_hash path; no PKCE code_verifier needed).
3. Ensure prod Site URL + additional_redirect_urls include app domain and /api/auth/callback.
Regression test: e2e - invitePlayer -> GET callback token_hash&type=invite -> assert redirect /me, player_ids contains invitee, invited[] cleared, user_metadata.invited=false; unit - assert inviteUserByEmail called with redirectTo.
Data remediation (after fix): resend invite to invitee-1 (unconfirmed user) or manually attach; ask invitee-6 which other emails they invited (only 1 recorded).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed with prod evidence; invitees who click invite link land on inviter's team and can enter their board; regression test added.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED via prod (dcfqzbdusxhrfgvnpwqc) read-only diagnostics 2026-07-28.

Evidence:
- Team 206 team 206: player_ids=[invitee-6 only]; invited=['invitee-1@redacted.invalid'] (still pending). Only 1 invite ever recorded despite 'people'.
