THE PAYING-CUSTOMER STEPS ARE OBSOLETE (amended 2026-08-03). The original runbook carried 'create real Polar product + webhook config', 'email the paying customer with a comp offer' and 'send the Polar checkout link'. v1 already migrated to Polar in production, so the products and webhooks exist. There is also no active Polar subscriber at all right now: the one paying customer is riding an unbounded 'pro' grace period with nothing behind it, to be resolved by hand on 2026-09-05 (wordle-teams-g3k). Drop those three steps.

What replaces them: whatever Polar subscription state exists at cutover must SURVIVE it, which means the v2 user has to resolve to the same Polar customer. That is an identity-mapping check, not a re-subscribe — and it runs straight into the identity bug described on wt-ksh.6, because every migrated user already exists as a Polar customer under their email.

title: Phase 5 — Payments (Polar)
description:
Polar checkout, customer portal, idempotent webhook handler writing webhook_events, upgrade/downgrade team-size mutations. See epic wt-ksh and the A1 amendment in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md.

NO LONGER GREENFIELD. v1 migrated Lemon Squeezy -> Polar in place and it has been live in production since 2026-08-03. v2 inherits the Polar orgs, the two Pro products (monthly + annual; Polar has no variants, billing cycle is locked at creation, so they are separate UUIDs passed as a products array to one checkout) and the webhook endpoints. Reference implementation: src/lib/polar/ on this branch.

PORT THESE THREE THINGS OR REPEAT V1'S BUGS:
1. events.ts mapEventToTransition - pure, no I/O, ports to Convex almost verbatim. active/uncanceled -> pro; revoked -> expired; canceled/past_due -> no change. Conflating canceled with revoked strips a paying customer's teams weeks before the period they paid for expires.
2. identity.ts resolvePlayerId - Polar does NOT reliably stamp external_customer_id onto a customer. When a checkout matches an EXISTING customer by email the value stays on the checkout and the customer keeps its own null external id. Webhook delivers, logs succeeded=true http=202, nobody is upgraded. Resolve customer.externalId -> checkout metadata -> checkouts.get(checkoutId), then repair the customer. THIS MATTERS MORE IN V2 THAN V1: at cutover every migrated user already exists as a Polar customer under their email, which is exactly the failing case.
3. Standard Webhooks ids are NOT UUIDs (msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W). Key idempotency on a STRING id read from the webhook-id HEADER, not the body. v1 lost time to a uuid column that rejected them and put Polar into an infinite retry loop.

VERIFY BEFORE ADOPTING @polar-sh/better-auth: v1 rejected @polar-sh/nextjs because its Webhooks helper auto-acknowledges, which destroys the store-then-process-then-500-so-Polar-retries behaviour the idempotency design rests on. The Better Auth plugin may do the same. Raw @polar-sh/sdk is the known-good fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox subscribe/upgrade/downgrade/cancel all mutate team limits correctly. PLUS: a checkout that resolves to a pre-existing Polar customer with a null external id still upgrades the right user (the v1 silent-202 failure), and a duplicate webhook-id returns success without reprocessing.

title: Phase 4 — Invites & onboarding
description:
Invite flow, invited-signup + add-player mutations, complete-profile flow, invite emails via Resend. See epic wt-ksh and the A2 amendment in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md.

v1 fixed its invite->join failure in July 2026. Two of its three causes were Supabase/Vercel specific and evaporate in v2 (the PKCE ?code= link that needed a code_verifier cookie an admin-initiated invite never planted; the scheme-less VERCEL_URL redirectTo that Supabase silently replaced with the Site URL — v2 already defends against that class via the SITE_URL fail-fast in fe81c46).

THE THIRD CAUSE SURVIVES THE REWRITE. invited[] was matched case-sensitively while auth stores emails lowercased, so anyone invited at a mixed-case address never joined. That is a data-model bug, not a platform bug, and a 1:1 port reproduces it. Normalise invite addresses to lowercase on write and compare case-insensitively on read. scripts/verify-case-fix-dev.mjs is the v1 proof and the shape to copy.

The claim in the design that handle_invited_signup 'is correct and is not the bug' was only true AFTER the case fix. Port the fixed semantics.

SCOPE THAT DISAPPEARS: the v1 plan's Option B — a branded invite email through the app's own infra instead of Supabase's dashboard template — was filed as a follow-up and never done. This phase does exactly that natively with Resend + react-email, so v2 supersedes it rather than inheriting it.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh email invited on beta lands on the right team with the right profile. PLUS: an invite sent to a MIXED-CASE address joins correctly from the lowercase account.

title: Phase 3 — Teams
description:
PHASE 3 OF THE v2 RE-PLATFORM. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-v2-phase3-teams-design.md. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-v2-phase3-teams.md.

WHAT WE ARE BUILDING AND WHY

Everything a team is, other than getting people into one: create it, switch to it, name it, set how it scores, see who is on it, take someone off it, delete it. Plus the two things this phase makes reachable for the first time and therefore has to settle - scoring-system versioning, so the editor cannot rewrite history, and a creator-only permission rule that is real rather than cosmetic.

Phase 3 is also the first phase with a second signed-in player available, so it closes wt-ksh.4.1, the one Phase 2 acceptance criterion deferred rather than met.

KEY DECISIONS, AND WHAT THEY RULED OUT

1. Pro gate: read it, gate the UI, enforce nothing. Phase 3 reads playerMembership to hide the scoring editor and to swap "New Team" for "Upgrade for more" past two teams. No mutation checks it. Ruled out enforcing server-side: v1's own gates are UI-only - its save action does not check pro, and nothing stops a free account creating five teams through the API - so enforcing would be a behaviour change rather than a port. Phase 5 owns whether that changes.

2. Scoring versioning: a scoringSystems table keyed on an effective-from month. Resolution for a month is "the row with the greatest effectiveFrom <= month, else the team doc's own eight fields". That fallback is what makes it need NO backfill and NO change to the copy script - "no version rows" already means "it has always been this", which is true. Ruled out snapshotting onto monthlyWinners (those rows exist only for months that have a winner and are deleted when nobody does, so a past month's scoreboard still has nothing to resolve against) and freezing months at close (adds a scheduled job and a correctness cliff if it ever fails to run).

3. Mid-month edits recompute the running month. effectiveFrom is the current month, so days already played this month re-score and the month's leader can change immediately. That is the literal reading of "applies to the current month forward", and the month is still in play - nothing anyone has been told is final gets rewritten. Ruled out applying from next month (the editor's effect is invisible for up to 31 days, which reads as a bug) and letting the user choose (a decision on every nudge of a number).

4. The version is surfaced by making the Scoring System card month-scoped: it shows the system that governed the month in the URL, badges it when historical, and hides Customize on a past month. Ruled out a separate version-history view and a note on the scores table.

5. Permissions: creator-only for every team mutation, enforced server-side via requireTeamCreator. v1's RLS permits UPDATE to the creator OR any member - including player_ids, so any member can remove any other member through the API - while its UI offers it only to the creator. v2 makes the UI's rule the real one.

6. Recompute blast radius: every affected month. Member removal recomputes every month the team has a winner row for; a scoring edit recomputes the edited month and every later one. v1's trigger fires only on daily_scores, so prod is carrying stale winners today.

7. One widened getMyTeams rather than a thin picker query plus a scoped detail query. The read set is the whole teams table either way (Convex cannot index array membership), so the split would double subscriptions without shrinking the read set.

8. The team picker is rewritten from Select to v1's DropdownMenu radio group, because "New Team" and "Upgrade for more" live inside the dropdown in prod.

9. Zero-teams state is a focused create-team card, not a port of v1's Intro marketing component. v2 already carries that copy at /about, amendment A7 makes onboarding a sanctioned parity exception, and this is the exact step where 87% of prod signups stall.

PREREQUISITE

teams.legacyId is a required v.number(), so createTeam cannot insert. Same problem and same fix as Phase 2's widening of dailyScores and monthlyWinners. Task 0, blocks every creation task.

SCOPE BOUNDARIES - EXPLICITLY OUT

- Invites and the InvitePlayer dialog. Phase 4.
- Polar, and enforcement of either gate. Phase 5.
- TeamBoards carousel, the monthly-winner celebration dialog, and the CheckoutReturn card. No phase owns these today; filed as wordle-teams-ry1, wordle-teams-k7w and wordle-teams-6tn. Phase 3 does not absorb them.
- v1's Intro marketing card.
- A teamMembers join table. The schema defers it until team count changes by an order of magnitude.
- Self-removal / leave-team. v1 has no such affordance.
- The pro month-history window. Phase 2 deferred that gate and this phase does not revisit it.

DIVERGENCES THIS PHASE ADDS - THE LIST GOES FROM THREE TO FIVE

4. Team mutations are creator-only, enforced server-side.
5. Membership and scoring changes recompute past winner rows.

Both are on the WRITE path and invisible in a static route-by-route comparison. V2-ADDENDUM 7a must record them before the phase closes (Task 14).

Scoring versioning is NOT a divergence: v2 had no reachable editor before this phase, so no v2 user has ever had a system rewritten in place.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. A multi-team account behaves identically to prod side-by-side. (Phase done-when.)
2. A player can create a team, switch to it, rename it, change its settings and delete it; can see its members; and can remove one.
3. A member who is not the creator is refused by the MUTATION, not merely by a hidden button - proven by test.
4. Editing a team's scoring system in August leaves July's month totals and July's winner unchanged, and July's Scoring System card shows which version applied.
5. Removing a member recomputes every month that team has a winner row for.
6. wt-ksh.4.1 - two browsers, two different signed-in players on one team: a board entered by one appears in the other's table with no refresh and no interaction.

GOTCHAS

Run everything from inside v2/. Import alias is #/. pnpm e2e is NOT part of test/tsc/build - run it after any task touching routes or rendered UI. Screenshot in light and dark on a TOUCH-EMULATING viewport before calling any UI task done. Do not commit while a subagent is running.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-team account behaves identically to prod side-by-side.

title: Phase 2 — Core loop
description: Board entry (port recent mobile keyboard/viewport work faithfully), scoreboard, month navigation, monthly-winner logic inside score mutation, access-check helpers. See epic wt-ksh.
acceptance_criteria: A full fake day works on beta — enter board, live score updates, correct monthly winner.
notes:
PARITY TARGET IS dev AS OF 2026-08-03, NOT THE 2026-07-16 SNAPSHOT. Two v1 behaviours changed after this design was written and a faithful port of the old code would be a regression:
 - a335ae8 board entry never loses a submission: handleSubmit wrapped in try/catch with setSubmitting(false) in finally, the sheet closes ONLY on success (it used to close unconditionally and discard everything typed), and a failed update_monthly_winners raises a warning toast instead of a silent success.
 - 45e3cd6 /me renders no browser-only state (hydration mismatch fix).
See amendment A3 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md.
PLANNED 2026-08-18. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md. Ten children wt-ksh.3.2 through wt-ksh.3.11, blocking graph wired.

Scope narrowed at brainstorm: the TeamBoards carousel, the monthly-winner celebration dialog and the pro gate on month navigation are all OUT, along with everything Phase 3 owns. Month navigation ships as a fixed three-month window, which is what v1 shows a free account.

Two NEW deliberate divergences from v1, on top of the duplicate-letter fix: the board upsert keys on (player, puzzleDay) so a double submit can no longer create a duplicate row, and hasSeenCelebration survives a winner rewrite when the winner has not changed. Phase 7's parity audit should therefore expect THREE known differences, not one.

A3's warning-toast behaviour is designed out rather than dropped: the winner write shares the mutation's transaction, so 'board saved but standings stale' is no longer reachable.
BUILT AND REVIEWED 2026-08-19, NOT YET VERIFIED ON BETA — do not close this epic until it is.

All ten children (wt-ksh.3.2 .. wt-ksh.3.11) are closed. Local state: 132 unit tests, 5 Playwright e2e, tsc --noEmit clean, vite build clean.

Design acceptance criteria 1,2,3,4,6,7 are met and verified in code. Criterion 5 (live update across two browsers with no refresh) is plausible but unproven — it rides on Convex reactivity, which nothing in the repo demonstrates end to end. Criterion 8 (a full fake day works on beta) is NOT met and cannot be met without a deployment.

Remaining to close the phase: deploy to beta, then walk the plan's Task 9 Step 6 — sign in as a copied account, enter a board, confirm the score appears with no refresh, open a second browser as a different player and confirm the first updates live, check the month total and ordering against v1 for the same data, and confirm the monthlyWinners row per team in the Convex dashboard.
CLOSED 2026-08-19 after owner verification on beta.

VERIFIED ON BETA BY THE OWNER: board entered on a real COPIED account; score landed in the correct cell with no refresh; monthlyWinners row present and correct per team; month totals and row ordering correct. Plus seven scores-table fixes found by the owner on a real phone after the first deploy (wt-ksh.3.12 through .3.18).

ONE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION DEFERRED, NOT MET: criterion 5, live update to a DIFFERENT player's browser. It needs a second team with a second player to sign in as, which Phase 2 cannot create. Deferred by owner decision to the end of Phase 3 and tracked as wt-ksh.4.1. The single-browser no-refresh check proves the mutation-to-query path but not cross-client push.

Final local state: 133 unit tests, 5 Playwright e2e, tsc --noEmit clean, vite build clean, deployed to beta and serving.

Fourteen follow-ups filed during the phase remain open. The two that matter before cutover are wordle-teams-7az (E2E_TEST_MODE must not survive onto the deployment that becomes production) and wordle-teams-04r (confirm Convex's backend clock is UTC — the today anti-spoofing bound depends on it).
