title: v2 re-platform: Cloudflare + TanStack + Convex
description:
# Re-platform to v2: Cloudflare + TanStack + Convex — Design

**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Status:** Approved design, pending implementation plan

## Summary

Rewrite wordle-teams as a new app (`v2/`) on a new platform stack, built in parallel
with the existing production app, tested at `beta.<domain>`, and cut over via DNS flip
when feature parity is verified. Strict 1:1 functional parity — no new features, no
redesigns — with two sanctioned exceptions: Convex reactivity making scoreboards
live-update (free win), and passkey enrollment (near-zero marginal cost inside the
Better Auth slice).

## Context & Drivers

- **Cost:** Vercel pricing grows steeply with scale; Cloudflare's curve is much flatter.
  Get ahead of growth.
- **DX/architecture:** the app is a client-heavy dashboard — TanStack's client-first
  model fits better than Next.js RSC/server actions.
- **Vendor reduction:** ~10 vendors today, ~6 after.

**Constraints:** ~40 DAU in production daily, small data, solo developer with a few
hours/week. Existing app must remain fully live and supported throughout. One paying
customer (~$2/mo Lemon Squeezy subscription) who must be personally migrated.

## Decisions Made (and alternatives ruled out)

| Decision | Chosen | Ruled out / why |
|---|---|---|
| Database | **Convex** | Neon — data layer must be rewritten either way (RLS + DB functions are Supabase Auth–coupled), so Convex's rewrite penalty evaporates; its reactive model fits a client-heavy dashboard best; generous free tier |
| Auth | **Better Auth** via `@convex-dev/better-auth` | Clerk/Convex Auth — user preference; open source; Polar has a first-party Better Auth plugin |
| Payments | **Polar.sh** via `@polar-sh/better-auth` | Built into new app from day one; no in-place Lemon Squeezy→Polar phase (only 1 subscriber) |
| Notifications | **No vendor** — Convex cron + `web-push` + Resend | Knock — one workflow doesn't justify a platform; Convex scheduling replaces both Novu and QStash |
| Strategy | **Vertical slices on a walking skeleton** (Approach A) | Layer-first (nothing testable end-to-end for weeks); strangler proxy on prod domain (sessions can't span two auth/db systems; machinery costs more than the rewrite at 40 DAU) |
| Repo | **`v2/` folder in this repo**, fully self-contained | Separate repo — same-workspace old code is superior reference material during porting |
| Beta data | **One-shot re-runnable copies** from Supabase | Live/two-way sync — sync machinery is where solo projects die; buys nothing at this scale |
| Parity | **Strict 1:1** | Redesigns/new features go to a post-cutover backlog |

## Target Architecture

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Framework | TanStack Start (Router + Query + server functions), Vite, React 19 | Server functions only where needed (webhooks, auth) |
| Hosting | Cloudflare Workers (TanStack Start Cloudflare target) | Wrangler; `beta.` subdomain during parallel run |
| Data | Convex — schema, queries/mutations, crons, scheduled functions | `@convex-dev/react-query` for live-updating TanStack Query data |
| Auth | Better Auth on Convex | Email OTP + Google, Azure, GitHub, Twitter/X + passkey plugin |
| Payments | Polar.sh via Better Auth plugin | Checkout, customer portal, webhooks |
| Email | Resend + react-email | Ports nearly as-is; also sends Better Auth OTP emails |
| Reminders | Convex cron → `web-push` + Resend | Replaces Novu + QStash + both reminder API routes |
| PWA | vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox) | Replaces Serwist; manifest ports as-is |
| Errors | Sentry (Cloudflare/TanStack SDK) | Wired from Phase 0 |
| Analytics/logs | Cloudflare Web Analytics; Workers Logs; keep LogSnag | Drop Vercel Analytics/Speed Insights, next-axiom, Axiom |

**Killed with no replacement:** Novu, QStash, Vercel KV, Edge Config, Lemon Squeezy SDK,
Serwist, next-axiom, Axiom.

**Open checklist item (verify in Phase 0):** whether Supabase Storage buckets hold real
user files (e.g. avatars). If yes → Convex file storage; if unused → nothing to do.

## Repo Layout & Environments

```
wordle-teams/            ← repo root unchanged; Vercel keeps building it
├── src/ ...             ← current Next.js app, untouched until cutover
├── supabase/
└── v2/                  ← new app, fully self-contained island
    ├── package.json     ← own deps, own pnpm-lock.yaml (NOT a workspace member)
    ├── wrangler.jsonc
    ├── convex/          ← schema, functions, crons, auth config
    ├── src/             ← TanStack Start app
    └── scripts/         ← copy-from-supabase.ts + parity verification
```

**Island rule:** no imports across the `v2/` boundary, no shared lockfile, no root
tooling changes. Old code is reference material only.

| Env | Hosting | Convex | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local dev | `vite dev` + `convex dev` | personal dev deployment | localhost |
| Beta | Cloudflare Workers | prod deployment of the project | `beta.<domain>` |
| Prod (post-cutover) | same Worker, promoted | same Convex project — beta *becomes* prod | main domain |

The beta Convex project becomes the prod project at cutover: final data copy overwrites
beta test data, domain flips. No second migration.

**Deploys:** GitHub Action on `v2/`-touching pushes → `convex deploy` + `wrangler deploy`.
Vercel's existing auto-deploy of `dev` continues untouched (never trigger Vercel manually).

**DNS:** nameservers move to Cloudflare early (free plan) — prerequisite for beta
subdomain and cutover; Vercel keeps serving apex/www through the same records.

## Data Model & Migration

**Tables (6, port near-1:1):** `players`, `teams`, `daily_scores`, `monthly_winners`,
`player_customer` (becomes Polar customer mapping), `webhook_events`. Docs keep a
`legacyId` for idempotent re-copying (or wipe-and-reload — fine at this size).
Relations become Convex ID references + indexes.

**Postgres logic relocation:**

| Today (in the DB) | In Convex |
|---|---|
| RLS policies | Access checks at top of each query/mutation, centralized in small helper functions |
| `handle_invited_signup`, `handle_add_player_to_team` | Mutations in invite/onboarding flow (Phase 4) |
| `handle_upgrade_team_invites`, `handle_downgrade_team_removal` | Mutations called by Polar webhook handler (Phase 5) |
| `update_monthly_winners` (trigger) | Logic inside score-submission mutation (transactional, so trigger semantics port cleanly) |
| `get_players_for_reminder`, `update_last_board_entry_reminder` | Internal functions called by reminder cron (Phase 6) |
| `custom_access_token_hook` (JWT claims) | Not needed — claims fed RLS; checks now read membership directly |

**Auth migration:** login is passwordless (email OTP) → no password hashes to migrate.
Copy script creates Better Auth users by email (+ name, verified flag). Sessions do not
carry over — the only user-visible cost of the entire migration is one extra login.

**Social OAuth:** trim to Google, Azure, GitHub, Twitter/X. Safe because OTP on the same
email is the universal fallback for users of dropped providers. Better Auth links social
logins to existing accounts by verified email; Twitter/X doesn't always return an email —
OTP is the fallback there too. Each provider needs OAuth app registrations with beta
callback URLs (during build) and prod callbacks (at cutover) — explicit checklist work
in Phase 1.

**Passkeys:** Better Auth passkey plugin + one "Add passkey" button in account settings.

**Copy script** (`v2/scripts/copy-from-supabase.ts`): reads Supabase with service-role
key, writes via Convex internal mutations. Re-runnable on demand; run once more during
the cutover window.

## Phase Plan

Each phase is independently shippable to beta, sized for 1–2 weeks of a few-hours/week
solo pace. **No phase starts until the previous phase's done-when is met.**
Phases 2→4 are strictly ordered; Phases 5 and 6 are independent of each other and may
interleave; nothing else may.

- **Phase 0 — Walking skeleton.** TanStack Start scaffold in `v2/`, Convex project,
  Better Auth email OTP only, deploy pipeline, `beta.` DNS, Sentry.
  ✅ *Done when: OTP login works at `beta.<domain>` and a page renders one value
  round-tripped through Convex.*
- **Phase 1 — Auth complete + data copy.** Full Convex schema, copy script (users +
  6 tables), social providers incl. OAuth console registrations, passkey plugin,
  account linking.
  ✅ *Done when: your real copied account logs in via OTP and via Google on beta, and
  enrolls a passkey.*
- **Phase 2 — Core loop.** Board entry (porting the recent mobile keyboard/viewport
  work faithfully), scoreboard, month navigation, monthly-winner logic in the score
  mutation, access-check helpers.
  ✅ *Done when: a full fake day works on beta — enter board, live score updates,
  correct monthly winner.*
- **Phase 3 — Teams.** Create/switch/manage, member lists, settings, team-scoped
  access checks.
  ✅ *Done when: a multi-team account behaves identically to prod side-by-side.*
- **Phase 4 — Invites & onboarding.** Invite flow, invited-signup + add-player
  mutations, complete-profile flow, invite emails via Resend.
  ✅ *Done when: a fresh email invited on beta lands on the right team with the right
  profile.*
- **Phase 5 — Payments (Polar).** Sandbox → Better Auth plugin, checkout, customer
  portal, idempotent webhook handler writing `webhook_events`, upgrade/downgrade
  team-size mutations.
  ✅ *Done when: sandbox subscribe/upgrade/downgrade/cancel all mutate team limits
  correctly.*
- **Phase 6 — Reminders & PWA.** Convex cron → reminder-eligibility port → web-push +
  Resend; vite-plugin-pwa, manifest, install/offline; old-Serwist-SW kill switch.
  ✅ *Done when: beta sends a real push + email reminder at the configured time and the
  PWA installs on a phone.*
- **Phase 7 — Parity audit + hardening.** Route-by-route walk of prod vs beta (static
  pages, `/me`, error states, sitemap/robots/OG images, maintenance page), fresh copy
  run + re-verify, cutover runbook written.
  ✅ *Done when: a written checklist of every prod screen has a ✔ against beta.*
- **Phase 8 — Cutover.** See below.
- **Phase 9 — Post-cutover cleanup** (~2 weeks after cutover). See below.

## Cutover & Rollback

**Pre-cutover (week before):** add prod callbacks to all four OAuth apps; create real
Polar product + webhook config; email the paying customer (what's changing, Polar link
coming, comp offer); in-app maintenance banner on prod ("you'll need to log in again");
one runbook dry-run (copy + verify, no DNS flip).

**Cutover day (target < 1 hour, low-traffic time):**
1. Prod → maintenance mode (existing `/maintenance` page)
2. Final copy-script run (beta Convex data replaced with real snapshot)
3. DNS flip: main domain → Worker; `beta.` stays alive on the same Worker
4. Smoke test on prod domain: OTP login, one social login, board entry, scoreboard,
   PWA opens on phone
5. Switch Polar webhook + OAuth primary URLs to prod domain
6. Send Polar checkout link to the customer
7. Announce done

**PWA continuity:** installs are domain-keyed and survive the flip; new SW takes over on
next visit. The Phase 6 kill switch ensures the old Serwist worker unregisters cleanly so
no one is stuck on a stale cache.

**Rollback (kept 2 weeks):** Vercel deployment and Supabase stay live and untouched;
rollback = flip DNS back. **One-way data rule:** scores entered post-cutover exist only
in Convex — rolling back loses them unless manually re-entered. Accepted at this scale;
breakage would surface within hours, not days.

**Post-cutover cleanup (Phase 9):** cancel/retire Vercel project, Supabase project
(after a final archived pg_dump), Novu, QStash, Lemon Squeezy store (after the
subscription is confirmed moved); promote `v2/` to repo root (old app lives in git
history); delete dead env vars.

## Testing, Error Handling & Observability

**Testing (proportionate, concentrated where rewrite risk lives):**
- **Convex function tests** (`convex-test` + Vitest), priority order: monthly-winner
  computation, invite/signup flows, upgrade/downgrade logic, access-check helpers —
  including negative cases (non-member *cannot* read another team's scores).
- **Parity spot-checks:** after each copy run, a script asserts row counts and known
  aggregates (e.g., a specific month's winner) match Supabase vs Convex.
- **UI:** manual and structured — each phase's done-when plus the Phase 7 route
  checklist. No component-test suite for a 1:1 port.
- **One smoke E2E** (Playwright: OTP login → enter board → see score) before each phase
  merge and on cutover day. One test, not a suite.

**Error handling:**
- Convex mutations throw `ConvexError` with typed codes; UI maps codes → sonner toasts.
- **Webhook handlers idempotent** (Polar retries): `webhook_events` dedup by event ID.
  Reminder cron never double-sends (last-reminder timestamp guard, ported).
- TanStack Router error boundaries per route section + root boundary → Sentry.

**Observability:** Sentry from Phase 0; Workers Logs for request logs; LogSnag continues
for business-event pings; Cloudflare Web Analytics snippet at Phase 7; Axiom dropped.

## Out of Scope

- Any new features or redesigns (except the two sanctioned: live-updating scoreboards
  via Convex reactivity, passkey enrollment)
- Live/two-way data sync between Supabase and Convex
- Zero-downtime cutover machinery (maintenance window is acceptable)
- Notification platform (Knock etc.) — revisit only if notification complexity
  materializes post-cutover
- Migrating Vercel-specific features with no user impact (Speed Insights, Edge Config)

## Acceptance Criteria (project level)

1. New app at the production domain on Cloudflare Workers with TanStack Start + Convex +
   Better Auth + Polar, at 1:1 functional parity per the Phase 7 checklist
2. All migrated users can log in (OTP or retained social provider) and see their full
   score history
3. The paying customer is subscribed via Polar; Lemon Squeezy retired
4. Reminders (push + email) fire correctly from Convex cron
5. Installed PWAs survive cutover without user reinstallation
6. Old stack fully retired within ~2 weeks of cutover; rollback path verified live
   until then
notes:
AMENDED 2026-08-03. dev was merged into feat/v2-replatform after ~93 commits of v1 work that post-date the design: the Lemon Squeezy -> Polar migration (now live in production), the invite->join fixes, and a run of performance/reliability fixes. See the Amendments section at the end of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md — several decisions in the body of that spec are superseded.

Headlines:
 - Phase 5 (wt-ksh.6) is no longer greenfield; v2 inherits live Polar orgs, products and webhooks, plus three hard-won bugs it must port fixes for.
 - Phase 4 (wt-ksh.5) inherits one invite bug that SURVIVES the rewrite: case-sensitive invited[] matching.
 - Parity is now against dev as of 2026-08-03, not the 2026-07-16 snapshot (wt-ksh.3, wt-ksh.7).
 - Phase 8 (wt-ksh.9) loses its paying-customer migration steps; Lemon Squeezy is already retired and there is no active Polar subscriber.
 - The COST driver is contradicted by the funnel data measured since. Open owner decision: wordle-teams-dts.
 - ALL OF v2 IS BLOCKED behind one manual owner step: moving wordleteams.com nameservers to Cloudflare (wt-ksh.1.1).
SEQUENCING SETTLED 2026-08-18 (closes wordle-teams-dts). Owner chose option (b): interleave funnel work with the port. See amendment A7 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md.

Three consequences for this epic:
 1. Cost is demoted from lead driver to secondary benefit. DX/architecture fit and vendor reduction (~10 -> ~6) carry the project. Not an open question any more.
 2. Strict-1:1 parity gains a THIRD sanctioned exception: the login/onboarding surface, alongside reactivity and passkeys. Rationale: wordle-teams-390 was re-measured 2026-08-17 and the leak did not move (163 -> 203 people reaching /login, conversion ~7% -> ~8%) even though Lemon Squeezy — A5's leading mechanical explanation — is gone. 93% abandon at login vs 87% at activation, with zero server-side auth failures. Porting v1's icon-only tooltip provider grid faithfully would reproduce the largest known leak in the product. Parity everywhere else is unchanged and still strict.
 3. Funnel instrumentation (login-page view, provider-button click, callback arrival) is a v2 deliverable, not a post-cutover backlog item.

This does NOT license a general redesign. Every screen outside login/onboarding still ports 1:1, and A3 still governs which version it ports against.

NEW PHASE INSERTED: wt-ksh.12, Phase 1.5 — Design system foundation, sits between Phase 1 and Phase 2 and now blocks wt-ksh.3. See amendment A8. Reason it goes here rather than later: v2/src/components has three files and no component library, so Phase 2 is the first phase to build substantial UI. Landing the design system after Phase 2 means restyling the board and scoreboard.

title: Task 13 — focused create-team empty state
description:
Plan task 13.

Replaces the Phase 2 placeholder ("Creating and joining teams arrives in Phase 3") with one card and one action.

NOT a port of v1's Intro, which renders the whole marketing About component with an animated gradient wordmark. v2 already carries that copy at /about, amendment A7 makes onboarding a sanctioned parity exception, and this is the exact step where 87% of prod signups stall (wordle-teams-456).

The zero-teams branch renders its OWN CreateTeamDialog - the one in the main return is unreachable from here, and the two must not both mount.

Files: v2/src/components/teams/empty-state.tsx (new), v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

pnpm e2e AND screenshots in both themes on a touch viewport.
acceptance_criteria: A player with no teams sees one card and one working Create Team button, and after creating lands on the new team with the team search param set.
close_reason:
Done in 92e7161 (empty state) and 3bf69dd (copy fix). Replaces the Phase 2 placeholder with one card and one action.

Review finding: the description promised 'You can invite people once it exists', but CurrentTeamCard has no invite affordance — invites are Phase 4 — so the very next screen silently failed the promise. On the one surface whose entire purpose is reducing onboarding friction. Dropped the clause rather than softening it to 'coming soon': this is the first thing a new signee sees, and naming an absent feature adds a claim they did not ask about.

Also updated login.spec.ts's assertion, which matched the old placeholder's exact wording, to target the heading role — net stronger, since it now also catches a regression where the card loses its asChild h1.

Separately filed wt-ksh.5.1: a cold signup has no players row, so this card's only action throws NO_PLAYER and reports 'Your session expired'. Pre-existing provisioning gap, Phase 4's to own.

209 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: CheckoutReturn card and the pro gates have no owning phase in the v2 port
description:
PARITY GAP WITH NO OWNING PHASE. Found while designing Phase 3 (wt-ksh.4), 2026-08-19.

v1's dashboard renders CheckoutReturn (src/components/checkout-return.tsx), which handles the return leg from a Polar checkout — including the case where someone upgrades before creating any team, where without it a slow webhook leaves them showing as free with nothing to trigger a refresh.

It belongs with Phase 5 (payments, wt-ksh.6) by subject matter, but Phase 5's recorded scope is the Better Auth/Polar integration, checkout, portal, webhook handler and the upgrade/downgrade mutations. This card is not named in it.

Related and also unowned: v1's pro gates themselves. Phase 3 reads playerMembership to gate the UI (scoring editor hidden for non-pro, "New Team" swapping to "Upgrade for more" past 2 teams) but enforces nothing server-side, matching v1, which is also UI-only. Phase 2 deliberately deferred the pro gate on month navigation, so v2 currently shows a pro user LESS history than prod. Whether Phase 5 enforces any of these server-side is an open decision for that phase.

Add to Phase 5's scope explicitly, or file as its own task.

Not blocking Phase 3.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 5's scope names CheckoutReturn and states whether the pro gates are enforced server-side.

title: Monthly-winner celebration dialog has no owning phase in the v2 port
description:
PARITY GAP WITH NO OWNING PHASE. Found while designing Phase 3 (wt-ksh.4), 2026-08-19.

v1 renders MonthlyWinnerCelebration (src/app/me/monthly-winner-celebration.tsx): the confetti modal shown to a team's members when a month closes with a winner, dismissed per-player via monthly_winners.has_seen_celebration.

Phase 2 WRITES the row this reads, including the deliberate rule that hasSeenCelebration survives a winner rewrite when the winner is unchanged (divergence 3 in V2-ADDENDUM 7a), but built no UI for it. Phase 3 does not reach it. Phase 7 is an audit, not a build.

So the data is correct and complete and nothing displays it. The dismissal semantics Phase 2 was careful about are currently unobservable.

Someone has to own it before Phase 7 runs, or it gets recorded as a deliberate cut.

Not blocking Phase 3.
acceptance_criteria: A phase owns building the celebration dialog, or it is recorded in V2-ADDENDUM 7a as a deliberate cut.

title: TeamBoards carousel has no owning phase in the v2 port
description:
PARITY GAP WITH NO OWNING PHASE. Found while designing Phase 3 (wt-ksh.4), 2026-08-19.

v1's dashboard renders TeamBoards (src/components/app-grid-items/team-boards.tsx): the day-by-day carousel of every teammate's board for the selected day, with the rule that a teammate's board is hidden until you have submitted your own for that day.

Phase 2's design listed it as Out of Scope ("Needs a carousel dependency"). Phase 3's scope is team management and does not reach it. Phase 7 is a parity AUDIT, not a build phase — it walks prod against beta and expects a tick against every prod screen. As things stand it will find this missing and have nowhere to send it.

Someone has to own building it before Phase 7 runs. Options: fold into Phase 3 as extra scope, give it its own mini-phase after Phase 4 (it is more legible once a team really has multiple players), or accept it as a deliberate cut and record it in V2-ADDENDUM 7a as a divergence rather than a bug.

Not blocking Phase 3.
acceptance_criteria: A phase owns building TeamBoards, or it is recorded in V2-ADDENDUM 7a as a deliberate cut.

title: Board-entry date picker is too small to use on a phone
description:
Reported by the owner from a real phone: the board-entry date picker is tiny and not very usable.

MEASURED CAUSE. v2/src/components/ui/calendar.tsx (stock shadcn, added in wt-ksh.3.10) sets [--cell-size:2rem] — 32x32px day cells. That is below every published minimum touch target:
 - WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), level AA: 24x24 CSS px absolute floor
 - WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), level AAA: 44x44
 - Apple HIG: 44x44pt.  Material: 48x48dp

It is also smaller than this app's OWN smallest control: DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 7 puts Button heights at 40 default / 36 sm / 44 lg. A 32px tap target is below the design system's own floor.

Compounding factors:
 - the trigger button is text-xs on mobile (sm:text-sm), so the label is small too — date-picker.tsx line 44
 - PopoverContent is w-auto p-0, so the popover sizes to content: roughly 7 x 32px plus padding, about 250px wide on a phone
 - on mobile the whole thing lives INSIDE the board-entry Sheet, whose height is bound to the visual viewport while the keyboard is open (the wt-ksh.3.10 keyboard-aware work), so it is cramped and can be clipped in the worst case

WORTH CONSIDERING, not prescribing:
 - raise --cell-size at mobile breakpoints so day cells reach at least 44px
 - a larger trigger label on mobile
 - whether a popover is the right container on a phone at all, or whether the date picker should present as its own sheet the way board entry itself does

PARITY NOTE: v1 uses the same react-day-picker calendar at default sizing, so prod is equally small. Making v2's materially bigger is a deliberate visual divergence — record it in docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md section 7a so Phase 7's route-by-route audit expects it rather than flagging it.

Verify on a touch-emulating phone viewport, not a narrow desktop window, and check it inside the board-entry Sheet with the keyboard open — that is the real context.
acceptance_criteria: Day cells meet at least a 44px touch target on mobile, and the picker is comfortably usable inside the board-entry sheet with the keyboard open.

title: Auto-scroll the scores table to centre the current day on landing
description:
FEATURE, requested by the owner during Phase 2 beta review. Small and self-contained.

On landing, the scores table should scroll horizontally so the CURRENT DAY's column is centred, rather than starting at day 1. A month has 28-31 day columns and only a handful fit on a phone, so today — the column anyone actually cares about — currently starts off-screen and has to be hunted for.

CONSTRAINTS, and the second one is the one that will bite:

1. AFTER HYDRATION ONLY. "Today" comes from the browser clock, and reading it during the render that has to match SSR is the hydration-mismatch class this phase has already been bitten by. useHydrated() exists for exactly this.

2. ONCE PER (team, month) LANDING — NOT on every render. The table is a live Convex subscription: it re-renders whenever ANY teammate submits a board. Re-centring on those updates would yank the view out from under someone mid-read, which is worse than never centring at all. Key the effect on team and month and guard it so it fires once per landing. Do not key it on the score data.

3. ONLY WHEN THE VIEWED MONTH CONTAINS TODAY. A past month has no current day; leave it at its natural position.

4. Do not fight the user. If they have already scrolled, do not re-centre.

5. Clamp to the scroll bounds so early- and late-month days do not leave a gap.

The cells already carry data-day="YYYY-MM-DD" (added in wt-ksh.3.11 so the e2e smoke test could address one cell), so the target is directly selectable — no positional arithmetic needed.

Behaviour is not unit-testable in this stack; verify in a real browser at a phone viewport, and check it does NOT re-centre when a board is entered in another session.
acceptance_criteria: Landing on the current month centres today's column; a live update from a teammate does not re-scroll the view.
close_reason: Closed

title: Every player row gets a bottom corner radius, not just the last
description:
Reported on a real phone: the player rows have a rounded bottom border, producing a small awkward curve at the bottom corners of rows that are not the last row.

CAUSE: in scores-table.tsx the corner radii are applied inside the rows.map(), so EVERY row's pinned cells get one:
  line 119  <TableCell className={cn(pinnedLeft, 'rounded-bl-md')}>
  line 150  <TableCell className={cn(pinnedRight, 'rounded-br-md')}>

Only the LAST row should carry a bottom radius. The header's rounded-tl-md / rounded-tr-md are correct as-is because there is exactly one header row.

This became visible with wt-ksh.3.16's switch to border-separate: under border-collapse the per-cell border was not painted by the cell, so the radius had nothing to curve. Now each cell paints its own border-b and the radius curves it on every row.

FIX: apply the bottom radius only to the final row. Either compute it in the map from the row index, or target it from tbody with a last-child selector — the latter matches how ui/table.tsx already cancels the last row's border ([&_tr:last-child>td]:border-b-0), so it keeps the two rules adjacent and consistent.

Check the result against the frame's own rounded-md corners; the cell radius and the frame radius must agree or the corner reads as a double curve. Both are currently md.
acceptance_criteria: Only the bottom row's corners are curved; intermediate rows have a straight separator edge to edge.
close_reason: Closed

title: Scoring system needs versioning so a change does not rewrite past months
description:
FEATURE, not a bug. Raised by the owner during Phase 2 beta review.

Today a team has ONE scoring system, and monthTotal is computed on read using whatever that system currently says. So editing the scoring system silently rewrites history: every past month's totals recalculate under the new values, and a month someone won under the old rules can change hands.

Desired behaviour:
 - a scoring-system change applies to the CURRENT month and all future months
 - past months keep the values that were in effect when they were played
 - someone looking back at a past month can SEE which version applied to it

This does not bite yet. v2 has no way to change a team's scoring system at all — the editor is part of team settings, which is Phase 3 (wt-ksh.4). Phase 2 deliberately left it out. The requirement therefore belongs with Phase 3, which is what first makes it reachable, and it should be designed BEFORE that editor ships rather than retrofitted after teams have edited systems in place.

Architecturally v2 is already well positioned: monthTotal, pointsFor and winnerOf take the scoring system as a PARAMETER rather than reading it from the team. Versioning can be introduced by changing what gets passed in — the pure functions in convex/lib/scoring.ts need no change at all. The work is in the schema (versioned systems with an effective-from month), in getTeamMonth resolving the version for the month being viewed, in recomputeWinners using the version for the month it recomputes, and in UI to surface which version applied.

Open design questions for that phase:
 - version by effective-from month, or snapshot the system onto each monthlyWinners row, or both
 - what happens to a month in progress when the system changes mid-month
 - whether existing teams get a single implicit v1 covering all history
 - how the Scoring System card shows historical versions

Note the v1 field name n_a is a misnomer worth correcting while doing this: v1's own Scoring System card lists it under "0 attempts", not "N/A" — it is the missed-day value, and has nothing to do with the N/A shown for weekends.
acceptance_criteria: Editing a team's scoring system leaves past months' totals and winners unchanged, and a past month shows which version applied.
close_reason:
Closed by wt-ksh.4.20 (scoringSystems table + systemFor/effectiveFromOf) and wt-ksh.4.25 (resolution wired into getTeamMonth and recomputeTeamMonth, plus setScoringSystem).

A scoring change applies from the month it is made forward; past months resolve to the version that governed them, falling back to the team doc's own eight fields when no version precedes them — which is why existing teams needed no backfill and the copy script needed no change. getTeamMonth returns systemEffectiveFrom so the card can badge a historical month; that UI is wt-ksh.4.29.

pointsFor, monthTotal and winnerOf were never touched, exactly as this issue predicted — versioning only changed what gets passed in.

The nA misnomer this issue also raised is handled in the UI: the row is labelled 'Missed day', not v1's '0'. Schema field name unchanged; it is the copy contract.

title: Scores table has nested scroll containers and the live one scrolls both axes
description:
Reported on beta: the whole scores table behaves as a scroll container. Everything in the component should stay put; only the day columns should scroll horizontally.

ROOT CAUSE, two parts:

1. NESTED SCROLL CONTAINERS. scores-table.tsx wraps the table in its own div with overflow-x-auto, and the shadcn Table primitive wraps <table> in ANOTHER div with `w-full overflow-auto`. The inner one is bounded by the outer and so is always first to overflow, making it the real scroller; the outer's overflow-x-auto never engages. Two nested scrollers with only one live is a recipe for scroll chaining and captured trackpad momentum.

2. THE LIVE SCROLLER SCROLLS BOTH AXES. The primitive uses `overflow-auto`, not overflow-x-auto, so the table can scroll vertically inside its own container instead of the page scrolling. That is most of the "weird behavior".

The pinned Player and Score columns are position:sticky inside the scroller and do stay put horizontally, which is the intended design and works — the problem is the container, not the pinning.

FIX: collapse to ONE scroll container that scrolls on the x-axis only. Keep the outer div as the bordered, rounded frame with no overflow of its own, and give the primitive's wrapper overflow-x-auto (it already accepts wrapperProps, added in wt-ksh.3.9 for the keyboard focus target). Verify the pinned columns and the keyboard-reachable scroll region both still work.

Note ui/table.tsx is a vendored shadcn component that v2 has already modified once; see V2-ADDENDUM section 6.

Found by the owner on beta after the Phase 2 auto-deploy.
acceptance_criteria: One x-only scroll region; the page scrolls vertically; pinned columns and keyboard reachability still work.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bare 'border' resolves to currentColor app-wide — Tailwind v4 default change
acceptance_criteria: A bare border utility renders the --border token in both themes, and the scores table border matches Card and Dialog.
close_reason: Closed

title: Verify Convex's backend clock is UTC — the today bound depends on it
description:
upsertBoardFor's anti-spoofing bound compares the client's today against toPuzzleDay(new Date()) evaluated on the Convex backend. toPuzzleDay deliberately reads LOCAL date getters (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate) rather than the getUTC* ones, because resolving "which day is this" in UTC is the v1 bug puzzleDay exists to fix.

The +/-1 day window is correct ONLY IF those local getters resolve to UTC on Convex's backend. That is very likely true — stripped V8 isolates without a timezone database default to UTC — but it is an assumption resting on a code comment, not a documented guarantee, and it is load-bearing for a security check.

Verify once against a real deployment: log new Date().getTimezoneOffset() from an actual mutation and confirm it is 0. If it is not, the bound is measuring against the wrong clock and the window may be wrong in one direction.

Raised in Phase 2 task 5 review.
acceptance_criteria: getTimezoneOffset() observed as 0 from a real Convex mutation, recorded in the issue.

title: convex-test cannot exercise the Better Auth resolution path
description:
convex/auth.ts throws at MODULE SCOPE when SITE_URL is unset:

  const siteUrl = process.env.SITE_URL
  if (!siteUrl) throw new Error('SITE_URL is not set on this deployment')

That fail-fast is deliberate and should stay — it guards against the scheme-less-origin bug where a redirect URL built from a deployment hostname silently sent users to the wrong place (see amendment A2 in the v2 replatform design, commit fe81c46).

The consequence is that ANY test importing auth.ts, even transitively, crashes at import time rather than at use. Phase 2 hit this the moment convex/access.ts imported authComponent: no prior test had pulled auth.ts into the module graph, so it had never been exercised. Worked around by setting SITE_URL in vitest.config.ts test.env.

That is fine for a value nothing dereferences. It will NOT be enough for the first test that needs a real Better Auth session — convex-test does not stand up the Better Auth component, so getAuthUser cannot resolve a user. Phase 2 sidestepped it by splitting each access helper into a form taking an explicit playerId (requireTeamMemberFor, playerForEmail), which is what the tests exercise, leaving the auth-resolving wrappers untested.

That split is good design on its own merits, but it means the auth-resolution path has no test coverage at all. Decide before a phase depends on it: either stand up the Better Auth component under convex-test, or accept that auth resolution is only covered by the Playwright e2e.

Not blocking Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded: either convex-test stands up the Better Auth component, or auth resolution is documented as e2e-only coverage.

title: v1 board over-demotes duplicate letters (production)
description:
Split out of wt-ksh.12.10, which fixed this in v2 only.

v1's getLetterColorsForWord (src/components/wordle-board.tsx) runs two passes; pass 2 demotes the EARLIER duplicate 'present' tile rather than the later surplus one, so a legitimate yellow is lost. Answer SPEED, guess GEESE:
  real Wordle:  - Y G Y -   two E's lit, matching the two in the answer
  v1 today:     - - G Y -   one
The player is told a correct letter is wrong, on the signature component. Live in production now.

WHY IT IS SEPARATE: the v2 branch treats src/ as untouched until cutover (design doc, Repo Layout), and v1 ships dev -> main, so a fix committed on feat/v2-replatform would never reach production. This needs its own branch off dev and its own release.

THE JUDGEMENT CALL, which is the owner's: v1 retires at cutover, so this is a fix to an app with a limited remaining life. Against that, it is small, it is wrong-answer-shaped rather than cosmetic, and current volume is 3-7 board entries a day from real people.

THE FIX: replace both passes with the standard two-phase algorithm — mark exact matches first, build a pool from the answer letters they did not claim, then walk the remaining columns left to right consuming from the pool. v2/src/lib/wordle.ts is a working reference implementation, and v2/src/lib/wordle.test.ts has the cases including a per-letter invariant (no letter lit more times than it appears in the answer).

NOTE: main is branch-protected — open a PR, do not push directly.
acceptance_criteria: In v1, answer SPEED with guess GEESE renders absent/present/correct/present/absent, and the fix is released to production.
close_reason: Won't fix — owner decision 2026-08-18. v1 retires at cutover and the bug is not worth a dev -> main release for the remaining life of the app. Fixed in v2 (wt-ksh.12.10), so it resolves itself at cutover. Reopen if the v2 timeline slips far enough to change that calculus.

title: v1 board over-demotes duplicate letters: a legitimate yellow is lost
description:
Found while porting the board in wt-ksh.12.6, by hand-checking a duplicate-letter case against real Wordle. Affects v1 in production TODAY and is faithfully reproduced in v2's port, pinned by a test.

THE BUG. v1's getLetterColorsForWord (src/components/wordle-board.tsx) runs two passes. Pass 2 demotes a 'present' tile to 'absent' when the running count for that letter has overshot AND a LATER column scored 'correct' for the same letter. It demotes the EARLIER present, not the later surplus one, so a legitimate yellow disappears.

WORKED EXAMPLE. Answer SPEED (two E's), guess GEESE (three E's).
  Real Wordle:  - Y G Y -   green at col 2, yellow at col 1, grey at col 4. Two E's shown, matching the two in the answer.
  v1 and the v2 port:  - - G Y -   only ONE E shown.
The player is told one of their E's is wrong when it is right. On the signature component.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED IN wt-ksh.12.6. Phase 1.5 is a strict parity port and the board is explicitly in the parity scope — A7's sanctioned exception covers login/onboarding only. Changing scoring feedback silently during a re-skin is exactly the kind of drift the parity rule exists to prevent. It is pinned by a deliberately-named test in v2/src/lib/wordle.test.ts so the behaviour cannot change by accident.

TO FIX: demote the LAST overshooting present rather than the first, or replace both passes with the standard two-phase Wordle algorithm (mark greens, build a remaining-letter pool from the non-green answer letters, then walk left to right consuming from the pool). The second is clearer and is what real Wordle does. Fix v1 and v2 together, or v2 alone if it lands after cutover; update the pinned test in the same commit.
acceptance_criteria: tileStates('SPEED','GEESE') returns absent/present/correct/present/absent, and the pinned divergence test in v2/src/lib/wordle.test.ts is replaced with one asserting real-Wordle behaviour.
close_reason:
Fixed in v2 2026-08-18. v1 deliberately left alone — see below.

WHAT CHANGED: tileStates now uses the standard two-phase Wordle algorithm — exact matches claim their letters, the remaining answer letters form a pool, and non-exact columns consume it left to right — rather than v1's two passes with a corrective demotion. Patching v1's pass 2 would have preserved a shape that is hard to reason about; this makes the invariant structural. Answer SPEED with guess GEESE now returns -YGY- (two E's lit, matching the two in the answer) where v1 returns --GY-.

VERIFIED ON THE RENDERED BOARD, not just in unit tests: GEESE against SPEED lights yellow at column 1 and green at column 2. Gate: build, tsc, 43/43 unit, 2/2 e2e. Deployed to beta.

THREE OF MY OWN NEW TESTS WERE WRONG, not the code — I had forgotten that an exact match in the middle of duplicates claims its column (ALLOY/BALLS is -YGY-, not -YYY-), that greens consume answer letters before any yellow can (ABBEY/BBBEY is -GGGG, not YGGGG), and my first invariant test compared a total against a single letter's count. Checked all expectations against an independent simulation before correcting them. The invariant test is now per letter: no letter is ever lit more times than it appears in the answer, which is the property v1 actually violated.

DELIBERATE PARITY DIVERGENCE, RECORDED. The board is inside the strict-parity scope and A7's exception covers login/onboarding only, so this is a knowing exception on correctness grounds: v2's board now differs from prod on duplicate-letter guesses, and only there. Phase 7's parity audit should expect that one difference rather than treat it as a regression. Documented in v2/src/lib/wordle.ts and section 7 of docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md.

v1 IS STILL AFFECTED IN PRODUCTION. Not fixed here because the design doc's Repo Layout rule treats src/ as untouched until cutover on this branch, and a change made here would not reach production anyway — v1 ships dev -> main, so it needs its own branch off dev and its own release. Whether that is worth doing for an app that retires at cutover is the owner's call; the fix is a small change to getLetterColorsForWord in src/components/wordle-board.tsx and this issue records the algorithm.

title: v2 header, footer and /about still carry TanStack starter content
description:
Surfaced during wt-ksh.12.4 rather than absorbed into it, since it is content, not colour.

The design-system migration recoloured these surfaces but deliberately did not touch their copy or links, which are all still scaffolding from the TanStack Start template:
 - Header wordmark reads 'TanStack Start'; nav has a 'Docs' link to tanstack.com; two icon links to x.com/tan_stack and github.com/TanStack.
 - Footer reads '(c) 2026 Your name here. All rights reserved.' and 'Built with TanStack Start', plus the same two TanStack social links.
 - /about is the template's 'A small starter with room to grow' copy about TanStack Start.

Not urgent — beta is not public — but it must not reach cutover. Note the real app bar (gradient wordmark, plan badge, avatar dropdown per DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 8) needs auth and team state, so the full version belongs to Phase 2/3; this issue is only about removing wrong-product content and putting the Wordle Teams wordmark in place.
acceptance_criteria: No TanStack branding, copy or links remain in v2's header, footer or /about.
close_reason:
Done 2026-08-18, verified on beta.

REPLACED: header wordmark (real green->yellow gradient, built from the brand tokens so v1's duplicated dark: variant collapses to one definition — drift #3 fixed by construction), nav (Docs and both TanStack social links gone), footer (v1's Feedback / Changelog / Support / About / Source Code / X), and /about (v1's actual copy including the 'not affiliated with New York Times' disclaimer).

ALSO IN SCOPE, same class of problem: public/manifest.json literally said 'Create TanStack App Sample'. Now Wordle Teams with the real wt-icon assets and favicon copied from v1, replacing the starter logo192/logo512. Phase 6 still owns the PWA machinery; this is branding only.

THE WORDMARK IS A LINK, NOT AN H1. v1 makes it an <h1> in the app bar, which gives every page a heading describing the site rather than the page, and would now collide with /login's own h1.

DELIBERATELY OMITTED: v1's Privacy and Terms footer links. Those routes do not exist in v2 and a footer of 404s is worse than a shorter footer — the static-page port is Phase 7's route-by-route walk. Likewise /about carries the substance of v1's page but not its eight screenshots or aceternity carousel; that marketing surface is Phase 7, and the carousel dependency is explicitly not being carried over.

CAUGHT A MISS FROM wt-ksh.12.4: the body had a hardcoded selection:bg-[rgba(79,184,178,0.24)] — the retired teal lagoon. That task's scan searched for token NAMES, so a raw rgba slipped through. Now selection:bg-accent-solid/25, and a value-level sweep (raw rgb triplets and hex codes from the whole retired palette, not just names) confirms nothing else remains in v2/src or the built CSS.

CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: the TanStack devtools badge visible in local screenshots is dev-only — 'TanStackDevtools' is absent from the production client bundle and beta's HTML has zero 'tanstack' occurrences.

VERIFIED ON BETA after deploy: /about title 'About - Wordle Teams', h1 'Wordle Teams'; /login title 'Login / Signup - Wordle Teams', h1 'Sign in'; no 'tanstack' in visible text and no tanstack links on either page; manifest serves name 'Wordle Teams' with 4 icons. Gate: build, tsc, 40/40 unit, 2/2 e2e.

title: Phase 8 risk: Microsoft users span 12 tenants, each with its own consent policy
description:
Surfaced while verifying wt-ksh.2.7 on 2026-08-18.

The 15 work/school Microsoft users in production span 12 DISTINCT Entra tenants (scripts/prod-azure-account-types.mjs). Consent is recorded in the USER'S tenant, not the app's home tenant, so the owner can only ever consent for directories they administer — in practice one of the twelve.

Those 12 tenants consented, under v1, to the scope set Supabase requested: email + offline_access (+ openid). v2 requests openid + profile + email + offline_access. The added 'profile' scope can trigger INCREMENTAL consent. Any of those tenants that disables user consent will then show its users 'approval required' with a justification box, and will need that organisation's own admin to approve.

This is unfixable from the application side. Scopes are already minimal — User.Read was removed precisely because it is a Graph permission and the most likely policy trip-wire.

Confirmed the shape of the failure on the owner's own work tenant (98825390-...), which has no prod users and therefore no v1 consent baseline: it demands admin consent for the app outright.

WHAT TO DO: do not attempt a code fix. Before cutover, decide whether to (a) accept that some Microsoft users may need their own IT to approve and communicate it in the pre-cutover email, or (b) drop 'profile' to match v1's consent surface exactly and backfill display names from another claim. (a) is preferred — profile is 'Admin consent required: No', so most tenants let users self-consent.

Affects at most 15 users; Google carries 236.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded before cutover, and if option (a), the pre-cutover communication mentions the possible approval prompt for Microsoft users.

title: X/Twitter OAuth for v2 needs a NEW OAuth 2.0 app, not the v1 one
description:
Blocker inside wt-ksh.2.6: 4 of 5 OAuth apps registered; X/Twitter outstanding because the existing app cannot be located in the X portal.

TWO INDEPENDENT CAUSES, verified 2026-08-17.

1. THE PORTAL MOVED. X app management is now console.x.com. developer.x.com/en/portal redirects there, and some legacy accounts report a redirect loop plus legacy 'standalone' apps not appearing / 'client-not-enrolled'. So the app may be genuinely unreachable, not mis-remembered.

2. THE OLD CREDENTIALS ARE THE WRONG KIND ANYWAY — this is the decisive one. v1 authenticates X through Supabase's LEGACY Twitter provider, which is OAuth 1.0a and uses API Key + API Secret. better-auth's twitter provider is OAuth 2.0: authorization endpoint https://x.com/i/oauth2/authorize, token endpoint https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token, PKCE code verifier, and authentication:'basic' on the token exchange (verified in @better-auth/core/src/social-providers/twitter.ts at 1.6.23). It needs an OAuth 2.0 Client ID + Client Secret, which the legacy app does not have until OAuth 2.0 is set up on it — and doing that mints new credentials regardless.

CONCLUSION: finding the v1 app saves only the app shell. Creating a fresh app in console.x.com is the shorter path.

CONFIG THE APP MUST HAVE:
- Callback: https://beta.wordleteams.com/api/auth/callback/twitter — path segment is 'twitter', NOT 'x'. better-auth's provider id is 'twitter' (id: 'twitter' in the source above). v2 serves auth from the TanStack route src/routes/api/auth/$.ts at SITE_URL, not from the Convex site domain.
- Client type MUST be confidential (Web App / Automated App or Bot). NOT Native App: a public client has no secret, and authentication:'basic' requires one.
- Email access must be enabled. better-auth requests scopes users.read, tweet.read, offline.access, users.email and reads user.fields=confirmed_email; without it emailVerified is false and account-linking-by-verified-email will NOT match the copied user — it would mint a second account, which is the exact failure wt-ksh.2.7 exists to prevent.

COST, NEWLY RELEVANT: X retired its free tier in Feb 2026 (secondary sources, not confirmed against official docs — verify before relying on it); existing free users moved to pay-per-use credits. better-auth calls GET /2/users/me TWICE per sign-in (profile, then confirmed_email). Production has 2 X users. See the decision issue.
notes:
RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-08-17: X is dropped from v2 entirely rather than registered. Four providers: google, azure, github, discord.

Safety verified before deciding, not assumed: scripts/prod-twitter-users-fallback.mjs reports 2 users with a twitter identity, BOTH with confirmed email addresses, 0 stranded. They reach the same account via OTP.

Gotcha for anyone re-running that check: filtering on the identities array alone returns ZERO twitter users. These 2 accounts carry no identities row; their provider only shows in app_metadata.provider. prod-auth-providers.mjs already handled this and the new script now mirrors it. A naive identities-only filter silently reports 'no X users at all'.

Plan amended: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-11-v2-phase1-auth-and-data-copy.md section 2.1.
close_reason: Superseded: X dropped from v2 rather than registered. See notes.

title: Hydration error on production /me, iOS Safari — separate from the $RS storm
description:
Split out of wt-uc5. While confirming uc5's root cause (back/forward navigation over a slow link re-running React's inline segment scripts), the production session replay showed a SECOND, independent defect that the back/forward mechanism does not explain.

Evidence, from replay 476e15be381d4acc84ab4ff10401e74b, environment vercel-production, iOS 18.7 / Mobile Safari 26.6 / iPhone, 2026-08-17:

  +3.84s  Meta / page load  https://wordleteams.com/me
  +3.85s  FullSnapshot
  +4.04s  breadcrumb navigation      {from:/me, to:/me}
  +4.29s  breadcrumb replay.hydrate-error  {url: https://wordleteams.com/me}
  +4.42s  Meta / page load  https://wordleteams.com/me   <- second document, 0.58s after the first
  +4.42s  FullSnapshot

replay.hydrate-error is Sentry's dedicated hydration-mismatch signal, so this is not inference. Two things need explaining and neither is the uc5 race:
  1. Why /me produces a hydration mismatch at all on this client. The 2026-07-30 fix addressed localStorage in useState initializers (see the comment in src/lib/contexts/teams-context.tsx:47-55) and that part holds, but 'const [month, setMonth] = useState(() => new Date())' at teams-context.tsx:55 still runs on both server and client. It normally yields the same month, so it is a suspect rather than a conclusion — a date-boundary or timezone-dependent render is the thing to look at first, and the affected user is US Central while Vercel serves from pdx1.
  2. Why the document loads TWICE in 0.58s. Not CheckoutReturn (it early-returns without ?checkout=success) and not a reload-on-controllerchange (no such code). The Axiom trail for the 2026-08-14 session shows the same shape — GET /login 307 -> /me immediately before the errors — so a middleware bounce is worth investigating: /me and /login are both matched, and a transient getUser() miss would produce /me -> /login -> /me.

Mutation analysis in the hydrate window: 489 adds vs only 4 removes, including a whole <table> with 33 <th> and 132 <td>. That is ScoresTable being inserted client-side rather than adopted from server HTML. Note the add-heavy shape means this is NOT React discarding the server DOM wholesale.

Replays are readable via: SENTRY_READ_TOKEN=<SENTRY_WRITE_TOKEN> node scripts/sentry-query.mjs raw "projects/christian-white/wordle-teams/replays/<id>/recording-segments/?download=true" — the org-scoped path 404s, the project-scoped one with the WRITE token works. Beware mixed units: breadcrumb timestamps are seconds, rrweb event timestamps are milliseconds, and reading them as one scale produces a nonsense timeline.

CAUTION ON MEASUREMENT: replays report count_errors 0 while carrying error_ids, and fetching those events returns 404 'Event not found'. Error events are being dropped, so Sentry issue lastSeen and event counts are NOT a reliable signal for whether this is fixed. Use the replay list.
acceptance_criteria: Identify what differs between the server and client render of /me for an iOS Safari client, fix it, and confirm no replay.hydrate-error breadcrumb appears in new production /me replays over several days. Separately explain or eliminate the double document load.
notes:
FIX APPLIED on fix/me-hydration. Scores are now attributed to the day it was in the SCORE OWNER'S recorded timezone, read from players.time_zone rather than from whichever runtime is rendering.

New src/lib/score-day.ts holds the rule: dayKeyOf(instant, zone) -> 'yyyy-MM-dd', dayKeyOfParts(y,m,d), todayKeyIn(viewerZone), HOME_TIME_ZONE = 'America/Chicago' as the fallback for the 8 production rows with no zone. String keys rather than Date comparisons on purpose — comparing two Dates for 'same day' means reading their parts, which is exactly the runtime-local trap being removed.

Changed: Player now carries timeZone (constructor, fromDbPlayer, and hydrate — hydrate matters most, since dropping it there would have the client fall back while the server used the real zone, recreating the mismatch); aggregateScoreByMonth takes an optional viewerTimeZone and matches days by owner zone; scores-table/table-config getData takes viewerTimeZone from useTeams().user; team-boards getBoardsForDate matches by owner zone.

VERIFIED, but only after discovering the harness was lying twice:

  TRAP 1 — PRODUCTION BUILDS ARE UNRELIABLE DETECTORS. A recoverable hydration error in a production React build does not surface to the console in a way Playwright reliably catches. Runs against 'pnpm start' returned 0/12 on code that was definitely broken. Everything measured that way is a false negative. Use 'pnpm dev', which prints the full mismatch including the differing text.

  TRAP 2 — THE TEST MUTATES ITS OWN FIXTURE. app-bar-base.tsx detects the browser timezone on mount and WRITES it to players.time_zone when the field is empty. So a Playwright run in Kiritimati silently sets the fixture player's zone to Kiritimati, and the next run measures different conditions. Pin players.time_zone to a fixed value before each run and confirm it afterwards.

DIFFERENTIAL (dev server, TZ=UTC; browser Pacific/Kiritimati so the client's calendar date is a day ahead; fixture player pinned to America/Chicago):
  unfixed: 1/8 loads, and 1/5 on the first attempt — roughly 12-20% per load
  fixed:   0/24 loads
At 12.5% per load, 24 clean loads is about 4% likely by chance; at 20%, about 0.5%.
The captured mismatch is React #418, a text mismatch in a ScoresTable day1 cell: server rendered 2, client rendered 0.
pnpm lint: 0 errors, 10 warnings — identical to the pre-existing baseline. pnpm build passes.

NOT CHANGED, deliberately: action-buttons/board-entry/form.tsx still uses isSameDay at :32 and :51. That code picks which date to PREFILL for entry rather than which day an existing score displays on, it is client-only so it cannot cause a hydration mismatch, and changing it would move where new entries land — a bigger behavioural change than was approved. Worth a follow-up so entry and display cannot disagree.

STILL OPEN, and NOT addressed here:
  1. The double document load, two /me loads 0.58s apart in the production replay. CheckoutReturn and a controllerchange-reload are ruled out; the /login 307 -> /me middleware bounce remains the lead.
  2. teams-context.tsx:55 still does useState(() => new Date()). Server and client read its month in their own zones, so near a month boundary they can disagree about which month the table is for — the same class of bug one level up, much rarer, untested.

REMEMBER THIS CHANGES DISPLAYED HISTORY. Measured on production: 582 of 7495 rows land on a different day under the player's own zone than under UTC. That is the point of the change, but it means some boards visibly move once this ships.

title: serwist defaultCache runs every navigation through NetworkFirst; its HTML rule is dead code
description:
Found while investigating wt-uc5 and rejected as that bug's cause, but it is a real misconfiguration worth fixing on its own.

node_modules/@serwist/next/dist/index.worker.js, defaultCache (used verbatim in src/app/sw.ts:20 as runtimeCaching):

  1. The pages/HTML rule matches on request.headers.get('Content-Type')?.includes('text/html'). That is the REQUEST's Content-Type. A navigation GET has no request body and sends no Content-Type, so this rule never fires. The 'pages' cache is therefore always empty — dead code upstream, not something we introduced.

  2. Because it never fires, document navigations fall through to the catch-all: matcher ({url:{pathname}, sameOrigin}) => sameOrigin && !pathname.startsWith('/api/'), handled by NetworkFirst into a cache literally named 'others', maxEntries 32.

So every same-origin page — including the authenticated, streamed, per-user /me dashboard — is stored in Cache Storage for up to 24h and served from there whenever the network fails. Two consequences worth thinking about even though neither is the uc5 crash:
  - A streamed RSC document is being buffered through cache.put on every navigation.
  - One user's rendered dashboard HTML sits in Cache Storage. On a shared device, an offline load could serve it after sign-out. Worth checking against the sign-out path, which has no obvious cache teardown.

Also note the SW is enabled for ANY production build (next.config.js: disable NODE_ENV !== 'production'), so preview deployments carry it too.

Suggested: pass an explicit runtimeCaching array rather than defaultCache, with NetworkOnly for navigations and RSC requests, keeping the static-asset entries. Confirm no offline-page expectation depends on the current behaviour first.
acceptance_criteria: Navigations and RSC requests are handled by NetworkOnly (verifiable in DevTools > Application > Cache Storage: no /me entry appears after loading it). Static asset caching still works and the app still installs as a PWA.

title: 5 of 6 accounts created since the 2026-08-03 release have never entered a board
description:
Activation gap found while checking whether anyone outside Christian's teams is using the app. Window: 2026-08-03 (prod release f476605) through 2026-08-14.

Since the release: 64 non-empty daily_scores rows by 7 distinct players. 6 of those 7 are on Christian's teams. Exactly one entry (1 board, 2026-08-05) came from outside them.

Six accounts were created in the window. Five have zero board entries:
  - A group of three signed up within 2 minutes on 2026-08-05 and formed a team. Only one of them ever scored, once, on day one. Nothing since.
  - One signed up 2026-08-10 via email OTP, completed their profile, reached the dashboard, and left ~90 seconds later. They never created or joined a team, so /me rendered the <Intro /> branch (src/app/me/page.tsx:44, the !teams || teams.length === 0 case) — a dashboard with no board to enter and no obvious next step.
  - One signed up 2026-08-14 via Google, completed their profile, created a team and sent one invite, then hit a client-side crash on /me (see wordle-teams-uc5) and the session ended.
  - The sixth is that invite, still unconfirmed.

Auth is not the blocker: every one of these confirmed and signed in successfully except the pending invite, and all five completed first/last name. They got in, looked around, and did not enter a score.

The zero-team Intro branch is the clearest lever — a brand-new user who does not create a team immediately has nothing to do.
acceptance_criteria: A new account with no team has a visible, single-click path from /me to either creating a team or entering a board. Re-run the since-release activity split and confirm at least one post-signup account enters a board without a nudge from Christian.
notes:
DUPLICATE of wordle-teams-456, which predates it (2026-07-30) and has far better data: 526 players, 458 of them (87%) never entered a board, measured across all of production. My version was filed 2026-08-14 from a 6-account sample in the post-release window and I did not check for an existing issue first.

Work the numbers in 456. The only thing here worth carrying over is the mechanism: /me short-circuits to <Intro /> at me/page.tsx:44 when a user has no team, so a signup who does not immediately create or join one has no board to enter and no obvious next step. 456 already suspects the invite->join flow (epic c0v) as a major contributor, which is a better lead than mine.

Superseded — do not work both.

title: New users hit 'Signups not allowed for otp' because Login and Sign Up are separate forms
description:
Production, 2026-08-10, real new user. First action on the login page was the Login form with an address that had no account. src/app/login/actions.ts:25 calls signInWithOtp with shouldCreateUser:false, Supabase returns 'Signups not allowed for otp', and the user is shown: "Login failed. If you haven't yet signed up, please try the Sign Up form."

They recovered (switched forms, account created 7 seconds later) but it cost an extra round trip and produced a prod error-level log for what is ordinary first-time behaviour. A first-time visitor has no way to know which of the two forms applies to them.

Options: detect this specific error and transparently route to the signup form with the address carried over; or collapse the two into one email-first flow that branches on whether the account exists. The error is already special-cased at actions.ts:34, so the branch point exists.

Related funnel leak, same window: on 2026-08-07 a Microsoft/Entra login was abandoned at the consent screen (/api/auth/callback?error=access_denied, AADSTS65004 'User declined to consent to access the app'). No account was created. Worth knowing the Azure provider asks for consent that at least one person refused.
acceptance_criteria: A first-time visitor entering an unknown address on the login page ends up in the signup flow without seeing a failure message, and 'Signups not allowed for otp' stops appearing as an error-level prod log for ordinary signups.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-17 on fix/signup-activation (8db474c), NOT yet deployed.

Approach: auto-switch rather than unify. login() returns needsSignup instead of an error, EmailSignin's Tabs became controlled, and the address is carried into the prefilled signup form with explanatory copy in the CardDescription. The alternative from the description — collapsing both tabs into one email-first flow — was deliberately NOT taken: it rewrites the whole entry point to fix a two-tab routing problem.

Branch on error.code === 'otp_disabled' (confirmed locally: status 422, code otp_disabled) with the message comparison kept as a fallback. log.error -> log.info for that branch, which is the second half of the acceptance criteria.

NOT fully transparent, by necessity: signup needs firstName/lastName for the update_player_names RPC, so the user still types their name. The failure message is what goes away.

ACCEPTED TRADE-OFF — email enumeration: auto-switching confirms an address has no account. The previous behaviour said so outright in the toast text, so this is not a regression, and the copy is neutral. Recorded here so it is a decision rather than an oversight.

VERIFICATION — differential, real server action against local Supabase on :54321:
  unfixed: all 4 hand-off assertions fail; captured toast is the exact prod string
           "Login failed. If you haven't yet signed up, please try the Sign Up form."
  fixed:   tab switches, address carried, no failure toast, hand-off copy present
  regression case: an address that DOES exist is not routed to signup and still
           shows a generic failure (uses existing-3io@example.com, created in the
           local DB via admin.createUser with email_confirm:true)
  pnpm lint clean in src/app/login, pnpm build passes

TWO TESTING NOTES worth keeping:
  1. Scope the signup email assertion to the panel containing 'First Name'. Scoping
     to the visible panel passes on unfixed code, because the login panel still
     holds the typed address. That produced a false PASS on the first attempt.
  2. Poll for toasts as they appear. Sonner auto-dismisses in ~4s, so checking after
     a fixed wait finds nothing and 'no error shown' passes when one was shown. Also
     allow ~10s on the existing-address path: gotrue blocks on an SMTP timeout
     because local inbucket is stopped. An 8s budget failed spuriously once.

NOT VERIFIED LOCALLY: the success path beyond this point (OTP actually sent, verification screen) needs SMTP, and local inbucket is stopped. That code is untouched by this change.

Harness: verify_signup_handoff.py in the session scratchpad, not in the repo (no test framework here, adding one was out of scope).

title: Monetization and marketing for earlier, more consistent Pro conversions — post-v2 roadmap #7
description:
# Post-v2 roadmap #7 — Monetization and marketing for Pro conversion

**Status:** stub. Needs the full brainstorming flow before any planning or code.

## What and why

Free members cost real vendor money, and that cost scales with growth while revenue
currently does not: today there is one paying subscriber. The goal of this epic is not
"more revenue" in the abstract — it is that Pro conversions arrive **earlier in a user's
life and consistently enough** that Pro revenue covers the vendor bill for free members as
the user base grows. Otherwise growth is a liability.

This is last on purpose: roadmap #2 (screenshot import) and #3 (global insights) are the
things worth paying for. Conversion machinery with nothing behind the paywall is just
friction.

## Open questions for brainstorming (not decisions)

- **Unit economics first, and this gates everything else.** What does one free *active*
  user actually cost per month across Convex, Cloudflare, Resend, Polar, Sentry? Convex
  database bandwidth is the binding limit (wordle-teams-dcu), and team chat (#1) plus
  insights (#3) both push on it. Produce a real number, then derive: at price P, what
  conversion rate covers N free users? That equation is the epic's spine.
- Price and unit of sale: per-user Pro, or a team-level plan where one person pays for the
  group? Team-level fits the product's social shape and may convert far better — one
  motivated organizer instead of five individual decisions.
- Free tier limits: what is the honest ceiling before restriction becomes rude? The free
  tier has to stay genuinely good, or invites (our only real channel) stop working.
- Trial versus freemium versus a metered taste of the paid features.
- Paywall moments: where in the flow does the ask appear, and does it land at a point of
  demonstrated value (just parsed a board, just saw a teaser insight) rather than at signup.
- Annual plan, and whether it is worth the support surface at this scale.
- **The referral/invite loop is the cheapest marketing we have** — teams are inherently
  viral and every existing user came through an invite. What makes inviting easier, more
  rewarding, and more likely? Possibly higher leverage than any pricing change here.
- Lifecycle email via Resend: welcome, activation nudge, dormant-team nudge, trial ending.
  Where is the line between useful and spam for a daily-habit product?
- Public pricing page and the conversion funnel it feeds (overlaps roadmap #5).
- Instrumented end-to-end funnel: visit → signup → activated → paywall seen → checkout
  started → subscribed, with time-to-conversion. Without this the whole epic is vibes.
- Churn, failed payments and dunning through Polar. Also confirm the first real checkout
  works (wordle-teams-7xl) before optimizing anything downstream of it.
- Grandfathering: the existing subscriber, and anyone who signed up under earlier terms.

## Explicitly out of scope until argued otherwise

Paid ad spend, ads or data monetization on the free tier, enterprise/B2B plans.
acceptance_criteria: Brainstorming complete and this epic body replaced with an approved design; child issues created for each atomic task; written unit economics stating the vendor cost of one free active user per month and the conversion rate at the chosen price that covers it; pricing/paywall/lifecycle changes shipped; signup-to-Pro conversion and time-to-conversion measured over a defined window and recorded on this epic.
notes: STUB EPIC — not ready to build. Post-v2 roadmap item 7 of 7. Do NOT start implementation from this body: run the full brainstorming flow first, replace this description with the approved design (scope, decisions + alternatives ruled out, out-of-scope), then create child issues per atomic task. Sequenced after roadmap #6. Depends on the two paid surfaces (roadmap #2 and #3) existing. Related: wordle-teams-dcu (Convex bandwidth is the binding cost limit), wordle-teams-7xl (first real Polar checkout).

title: PWA launch screen and startup speed — post-v2 roadmap #6
description:
# Post-v2 roadmap #6 — PWA launch screen and startup speed

**Status:** stub. Needs the full brainstorming flow before any planning or code.

## What and why

For the people who actually use this daily, the installed PWA *is* the app. Right now
tapping the icon gives you an unbranded blank hold before anything appears — it reads as
broken, every single day, to exactly the users we most want to keep.

Two halves, and they are worth doing together because they are the same perceived moment:
give the launch a branded splash, and make the time behind it short.

wt-ksh.7.1 covers replacing the scaffold manifest with real Wordle Teams identity as part
of v2 itself. This epic is the polish pass beyond that: splash imagery across devices, and
actual startup performance work.

## Open questions for brainstorming (not decisions)

- **Profile before optimizing.** Where does cold start actually go: bundle download, JS
  parse, the auth round-trip, or the first Convex query? Guessing here wastes the whole
  epic. Measure on a real mid-range phone on cellular, not a desktop with fast 3G throttle.
- iOS splash screens: Safari still wants per-size `apple-touch-startup-image` links. Hand
  produce, or generate the set at build time from one source asset?
- Android/Chromium derives its splash from the manifest (icon, name, theme and background
  color) — verify those produce something we actually like.
- Maskable icons, and how the icon looks in every launcher shape.
- **App shell that renders instantly**: paint the board frame, nav and team name before
  auth and Convex resolve, instead of holding a blank screen until data lands. Decide
  skeleton versus spinner versus optimistic last-known state cached locally.
- Can the previous session's board render from cache on launch and reconcile when Convex
  connects? Biggest perceived-speed lever if the data model allows it.
- Service worker precache strategy under vite-plugin-pwa/Workbox: what is precached, what
  is runtime-cached, and how updates roll out without a stale-app trap.
- Offline behavior: what should tapping the icon with no signal actually show?
- A defined performance budget and a way to notice regressions later.

## Explicitly out of scope until argued otherwise

Native app wrappers or app store submission, push notification work (Phase 6 owns that),
broad visual redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Brainstorming complete and this epic body replaced with an approved design; child issues created for each atomic task; branded launch screen present on installed iOS and Android; cold-start time from home-screen icon tap to interactive board measured on a real mid-range phone before and after, with both numbers recorded on this epic.
notes: STUB EPIC — not ready to build. Post-v2 roadmap item 6 of 7. Do NOT start implementation from this body: run the full brainstorming flow first, replace this description with the approved design (scope, decisions + alternatives ruled out, out-of-scope), then create child issues per atomic task. Sequenced after roadmap #5 (SEO). Related: wt-ksh.7.1 (PWA manifest identity, v2-scoped), wordle-teams-jcj.

title: SEO — post-v2 roadmap #5
description:
# Post-v2 roadmap #5 — SEO

**Status:** stub. Needs the full brainstorming flow before any planning or code.

## What and why

Organic acquisition is currently close to nothing, and the v2 stack makes that worse by
default: TanStack Start is client-first, so nothing is indexable unless we deliberately
prerender it. Every user we have came from a personal invite. Invites are the cheapest
channel and will stay the main one (roadmap #7), but they only compound if strangers can
also find the product.

Doing this after cutover is deliberate — the marketing surface gets rebuilt on Workers
anyway, so tuning v1's pages would be thrown away.

## Open questions for brainstorming (not decisions)

- **What are we even trying to rank for?** "wordle with friends", "wordle leaderboard",
  "wordle group scores" — needs actual keyword research, not intuition. If the realistic
  ceiling is tiny, the honest answer may be "do the hygiene, skip the content strategy."
- Which routes get prerendered or SSR'd on Cloudflare Workers, and which stay
  client-only. The app itself should not be indexed; the marketing and explainer surface
  should.
- Metadata, OG and Twitter cards per route — social preview quality matters more than
  ranking for an invite-driven product, since every shared link is a preview.
- sitemap.xml and robots.txt, generated rather than hand-maintained. v1 shipped
  /maintenance in its sitemap (wordle-teams-ef9); do not recreate that class of bug.
- Structured data — is any of it applicable, or is it cargo cult here?
- **Content that only we can write:** aggregate pages from the global corpus (hardest
  answers, opening-word performance) would be genuinely unique and link-worthy. Direct
  overlap with roadmap #3 — decide whether insights ship a public tier.
- Core Web Vitals on the Workers build, and Cloudflare cache/CDN configuration for the
  static surface. (v1 had unexplained ~2.2s server time on prerendered marketing pages,
  wordle-teams-jcj — do not inherit it.)
- Canonical domain and URL preservation post-DNS-flip: any v1 URL that has ever been
  linked needs a 301, and there must be exactly one canonical host.
- Search Console and Bing verification on the new deployment; analytics attribution for
  organic sessions.

## Explicitly out of scope until argued otherwise

Paid acquisition, blog/content mill, backlink outreach, app store presence.

title: App onboarding tour — post-v2 roadmap #4
description:
# Post-v2 roadmap #4 — App onboarding tour

**Status:** stub. Needs the full brainstorming flow before any planning or code.

## What and why

New users arrive and are not told what to do. 87% of production signups have never
entered a single board (wordle-teams-456) — 458 accounts. Part of that is the invite→join
bug that has since been fixed, and part of it is that the app assumes you already know
the model: that you enter *your own* board each day, that your score is compared against
teammates over a month, that you need a team before any of it means anything.

By the time this ships, v2 will have removed the platform excuses and the login lockout
(wordle-teams-jvt) will be gone. This epic is the product-side half of the activation
problem: make the first two minutes explain themselves.

## Open questions for brainstorming (not decisions)

- **Tour versus guided doing.** A tooltip carousel is the easy build and the weak outcome.
  Alternatives to weigh: progressive empty states that instruct in place; a scripted
  first-board walkthrough where the user actually enters a real board with help; a
  one-screen "here's the idea" before the first play. Guided doing usually beats narration.
- **Different entry paths need different first actions**, and this is the crux:
  - invited user joining an existing team → their first action is enter today's board;
  - self-signup with no team → their first action is create a team and invite someone;
  - team creator → their first action is get a second human in the room.
  A single linear tour serves none of them well.
- Where the real drop-off is: we do not yet know whether people stall before creating a
  team, before inviting, or before entering a board. Instrument first, or design against
  the v1 evidence we have? (Related: wordle-teams-390's ask for funnel events.)
- Skip, resume, and never-show-again semantics; where the "seen" flag lives; how a user
  replays it later.
- Per-step analytics so the tour itself can be debugged — a tour we cannot measure is a
  guess we cannot correct.
- Mobile-first: login traffic is heavily iPhone. Anything hover-dependent is dead on
  arrival (the tooltip-only OAuth labels in v1 are the cautionary tale).
- Library versus hand-rolled, given the v2 stack.
- Does the empty scoreboard state itself carry most of the load, making the tour smaller?

## Explicitly out of scope until argued otherwise

Marketing-site explainer content (roadmap #5), lifecycle re-engagement email (roadmap #7),
in-app help center.
acceptance_criteria: Brainstorming complete and this epic body replaced with an approved design; child issues created for each atomic task; per-step completion events instrumented so drop-off is attributable to a specific step; activation rate (signup to first non-empty board) measured for a defined window before and after launch, with the numbers recorded on this epic.
